talks.content: Welcome back. What are your plans for today? Or are you planning to rest at home?

options.content: Do you have any wishes, Berry?
It's so bitterly cold here in Icelake...
Berry? How come you are here?
You've always preferred quiet settings; does the noise here bother you?

talks.content: Wishes? I... can't think of any. Your smile in the morning is already the greatest pick-me-up of all.
Unlike Purgatorio Island, it snows here every day. Thankfully, you have a warm place to stay. Compared to our little shack back on the island, this place feels quite luxurious.
...I'm not sure either. Maybe it's a beautiful dream where I've never left your side, as always.
Well, that place is like a city made of steel... Mm, more like a prison, to be precise. I spent my early years there.
It's somewhat noisy, but I don't hate it. You've made many new friends here, which is a good thing — I'm really happy for you.
Then rest your head on my lap for a while, just like old times.
I promise I'll get you back.
But I'm still a bit chilly.
I'd give anything to see you again.
Later on, along with you, I was taken away from there by someone, and we ended up on Purgatorio Island. I can't share much about her, though — Sorry, I promised her.
This way, you'll never feel lonely, even when I'm not around.
Don't push yourself. If you ever feel down, just come to me for a chat. Or, if you don't feel like talking, we can just spend some quiet time together.
Remember how your hands would always get very cold in winter? Here, let me warm them up.
I feel the same, very much so... May we truly reunite one day.

...Life on Purgatorio Island was so peaceful, that I almost believed we could live that way forever. But it wasn't until the day they came for me that I realised I had never truly escaped that prison.
I assume the role of the shattered prisoner, and you, as a watchful warden, stand sentinel over my chains.

options.content: Could you tell me about Blues?
I look forward to the day you embrace your birth name once more.
Do you have any wishes left? Let me know if I can be of any help.
Can you teach me how to act?
Could you tell me about the Galea Theatre?

talks.content: He was a shattered crystal lamp, a fallen star plunged into a filthy gutter.
Why should I? Parsifal's story ended long ago. That name is but a distant echo now, so faint and far away that I sometimes wonder if it was ever real.
You're so kind. Thank you. Yet, all my vows have been fulfilled. There's little left that stirs my heart.
Why seek to learn acting? You have no need to become someone else.
It stands, enduring time far beyond my years. On one side of its towering walls lies the imposing inner city — majestic as storm clouds, yet colder.
But to me, you're real.
Become someone else?

Elegantly clad figures alight from silk-lined carriages, discussing art, poetry, and the perpetual gloom of the skies. They gossip about balls and betrothals, lamenting how the mire of melting snow from the outer city soils their fine leather boots.
He was just like those things — laughably absurd, yet somehow, they shine brilliantly.
...Is that so?
Should you ever find yourself at the Galea Theatre, please convey to Ms Violetta that I've settled down in Aethyrie. Assure her not to worry, as I am doing very well now.

When you're on stage, every part of you — from your very bones to the breaths you take — is surrendered to the character. In that moment, you can shed all your sorrows and pain, stepping into a world unblemished by reality.

On the other side of the walls, the rowdy fog district buzzes with chaos. Vendors hawk loudly, mothers clutch their children, begging for a scrap of rye bread. Mischievous hands sketch defiant graffiti, always a step ahead of the patrols.

The wall between our cells was so thin, every sound passed through. There he was, barely a metre away — rambling about his family, spinning dreams of the future, or singing some hopelessly off-key tune.
Then I shall carry this final performance to its conclusion — for you, my last and only audience.
"A land of music and poetry, where every pebble taps out a rhythm, and every brook sings a melody."
But you... you were born the {性别：hero|heroine} of your own story, already carrying the admiration and trust of those around you. You shine effortlessly, needing no spotlight to dazzle.
And so stands our Galea Theatre, caught between these two worlds, hearing all yet understanding none.
For a moment, I'd forget I was a caged beast. Instead, I'd feel like an ordinary child in school, waking from a nightmare during an afternoon nap to the racket of a noisy classmate beside me.
Thank you, for granting me a stage to rest my weary soul.
Hopefully, that'll keep her from enquiring after me. Once her favoured pupil... I'd rather not tarnish her memories.
Any personal memories there?
So, you were drawn to him, and you became friends.
A little white lie, I see.
Oddly, it's not the scripts or the lavish costumes that first come to mind, nor the cluttered prop room I swept daily.
...Heh. Perhaps.
Indeed. Ignorance is always bliss.

It's the velvet carpet that blanketed the stage after the curtain fell. As a child, after the earliest performance I can remember, my mother and I lingered on the stage after everyone left, reciting lines and dancing through the night.
But "friend" is far too bright a word for someone like me. We were more like two stranded fish, floundering together in a drying riverbed.
When dawn broke, exhaustion finally overtook me. I lay down on that carpet, resting my head on Mother's lap, and drifted into a long, sweet dream.
Hey! I'm taking Samael out for some fresh air — soaking up the sunlight, getting a feel for this place together. Wanna say hi? It'll be thrilled! ...Well, probably! Hehe~

options.content: So... what are the Church folks like?

talks.content: Samael's not just a weapon — it's my best friend!
Ugh—! Shut up! I don't want to talk about those old stick-in-the-muds! Ughhh, you've ruined my day— ...No, no, I can't get angry. Stay calm, Lisbell...
Just what it says. Being patient means staying strong and stoic — putting up with anything and never, ever blowing up!
The "Seven Virtues" are the most noble, most powerful, and most drop-dead dazzling champions in all of Elysium! Naturally, they're also the most virtuous — it's in the name!
Why would you call a sword your friend?
Sounds like you've got some issues with them.
That sounds... really tough.
Uh...

In the Church, only those chosen by one of the Seven Relics can become one of the "Seven Virtues." There were loads of strong warriors that day, but I was the only one who could pull Samael free. It chose me, so of course I've got to treat it right!

Ahem! Not at all! They are absolutely wonderful. So kind and understanding. When you mess up a hymn, you just have to copy it thirty times. And if they catch you feeding cream to Samael, it's only two days locked up for solitary reflection. Really, they're the best. Absolutely lovely...

Right!? But because of this title, they're always telling me to "swallow my anger with patience." But it's like... like being forced to stop mid-yawn or raising your sword for a perfect strike, only to be told, "Hey! That's not an enemy, it's a friend!" It just makes you even more—
What's with that look...? How dare you doubt me! I hereby sentence you to copy the Codex thirty — no, a hundred times!
...Only thing is, ever since then, it hasn't responded to me. Not once... W—Wait — that's top secret! You can't tell anyone, got it!?
Argh, they say anger is a grave sin. I mustn't get angry. I mustn't...
You smother its blade in ice cream every day. No wonder it's giving you the silent treatment.
That must be hard on you.
Huh!? It doesn't like ice cream!? Then... what about mashed potatoes? Or salad dressing!?
Well... it comes with the job! I am Lord Patience, after all! Hehe!
Ah, it's you, my dear child. Good day. Is there something on your mind you'd like to share with me?

options.content: From your attire, you don't appear to be from Hyperborea.
Could you tell me about the Misty Sea?
I never expected you to be so skilled in battle.
Could you tell me about your friends?

talks.content: Indeed. Over the course of endless time, I've travelled — or perhaps wandered — through every corner of Atlasia, treading upon every inch of its soil and tracing every grain of sand with my fingertips.

The Misty Sea is the birthplace and final rest of all living beings. To the Misty Sea, the deceased return, and from there, life begins anew... just as dying clouds dissolve into the earth as rain, only for flowers to bloom again from that very soil.
Did that surprise you? Long ago, during the Great Migration, I stood on the front lines as a soldier well-versed in close combat.
"Friends"... By the common definition of the word, I've had many over my long years.
So, which place is your favourite?
Will I go there someday, too?
Though those days are far behind me, I still remember the essentials of fighting.
Yet when I hear that word, the first who come to mind are Lexis and Erika, the two who once led me away from Elysium.

Once you've seen enough, you'll find that the scenery of all places is not so different after all. Whether it's the snows of the North, the sands of Khemet, or the smoke curling from the chimneys of Huaxu, they are all but different shades of mist drifting through the forest.
I believe so, my child. One day, you will journey to the Misty Sea, into the embrace of Mother Embla.
During my wanderings, I've often faced roaming beasts. Their claws and fangs have left me with scars, bruises, and even deaths I should have rightfully endured.
What were they like?
If I had to choose, though... it would be the mountains and forests of Aethyrie. The air there brings me the most peace.
That sounds... a bit scary.
It's hard to picture you grappling hand-to-hand...
In the annals of history and the tales of heroes, they're often portrayed as the Sage who tore away the gods' veil of ignorance, and the Heroine who gave her life for the Sage's cause...
I'll have to visit someday.
My dear child, cherish all that life offers, yet do not shrink from its passing. Demise is not suffering, but the inevitable conclusion of life's journey.
Even the eternal moon wanes and waxes, ever changing. Humans, naturally, are far more complex — especially one who's lived countless lifetimes beyond a mortal span.
But in my memories, they are simply Lexis and Erika.
Perhaps you will.
Should you ever grow weary, rest in my arms for a while... There is no need to fear — this will not be your eternal sleep. There is still much for you to fulfil in this world.
If you're curious about those days, I'll recount them in detail for you another time.

Erika was a brave and lively young woman, with a spirit that drew everyone to her. Lexis, though brilliant, often overthought things. He'd suddenly lapse into deep musings, which, ironically, made him seem a bit slow.
Should you wander into the Emerald Forest, would you mind bringing a bouquet of white asters for me? Beneath its earth rest my friends, my child, and a version of myself from long ago.
Any fun stories?

Mm... There was one time Lexis tried to apologize to Erika for something he'd done. On a whim, she pointed to one of the soldiers' archery training dummies, saying she'd forgive him if he could hit the bullseye...
Of course, she didn't mean it seriously. Not even all the soldiers could manage it, let alone Lexis, whose hands were meant for quills and scrolls, not bows or blades.
But he took her words to heart. After the soldiers left, he stayed behind and practised alone, long into the night.

As you might guess, true history is not a tale of omnipotent heroes. Even someone as brilliant as Lexis had his limits — he practised until his palms bled. Erika ended up wrapping them in linen, but he never did strike the mark.
The funny thing is, I can't even recall why they argued in the first place. Strange, isn't it? When I think of them now, it's always these small, insignificant details that come to mind first.
Sounds like some golden memories.
Indeed. Those were such precious, joyful days... But they are far behind me now.

Today's perfect for drinking and singing! Come on, let me finish this glass, and then we'll chase down the sinners who deserve my sword. What? I said the same thing yesterday? Well, every day's a fine day to live like this, don't you think?

options.content: I hear your swordsmanship is remarkable.
Why would you rebel against Huaxu's laws?
You seem to use all sorts of weapons besides the sword. Can you still call yourself a swordsman?
I heard people who practice martial arts like you all have some kind of titles or nicknames. Is that true?

talks.content: You're into swordplay too? Figured as much — you've got a fine blade there. You must be pretty good with it. Let's have a friendly spar and see what you've got!
Plenty of reasons, really, but if I had to sum it up: I hate being bound by them.

Of course! Being good with a sword doesn't mean you're stuck using only it. In Huaxu, there are people who can use pens and chopsticks as weapons — does that mean swordsmen are supposed to starve or never write?

They sure do. Now that you mention it, I can think of quite a few. Stuff like "King So-and-So," "Lord Something," or "Immortal This-and-That." Animals are the go-to — dragons, tigers, lions, cranes, you name it. It's like a whole zoo out there.
Honestly, it's been ages since I've met anyone truly on par with me. Though, my shifu always said I need more honing because I'm too blunt — and that I should work on my acting.

I've been free-spirited all my life, doing everything my way, drawing my sword wherever I saw injustice. I only ever listened to what I wanted to hear from my Shifu or Yuming. The rest? In one ear and out the other, like the wind passing by. So tell me, why would I let myself be chained by some laws?
That's disappointing. I was hoping you could do stuff like slicing a bullet in half with your sword.

Here's how it works: the longer the title, the lousier the skills. Four words? A newbie. Three? Not bad. Two — that's someone you don't want to mess with. And those with no nickname at all? They're the true grandmasters.
Is acting part of swordsmanship?
Tell me the biggest reason then.
Oh, I can do that. But why bother? Dodging is way easier, after all. Even boars in the woods know to go for radishes over tree bark when they can.
So is Kezhou your real name or a nickname?

Not exactly how I see it, but he always said that swordsmanship isn't just about skill; it's about strategy. Stuff like "conceal your strength by feigning weakness," "subdue the enemy without fighting," and "overwhelm the few with the many." Said that's what separates the good from the great.

I'd say it's the concern of a swordsman. Think of it this way — when you first learn swordsmanship, you follow the swordplay scroll move by move, right? Against regular foes, that's enough. Your sword moves instinctively.
That said, if I ever meet a worthy opponent, you can bet I'll draw my sword and go all out.

I walk this world with my real name, of course. I know, it sounds made-up, doesn't it? Even my shifu used to say so — warned me that a name like this would have people mistaking me for some prodigy, and that'd only bring me trouble.

Back when I was a kid, he used to pull that same trick on me. He'd claim his skills were mediocre and tell me if I could knock him down, I wouldn't have to train anymore. Took me a whole year to realize I couldn't even touch his sleeve.

But if you stick too closely to the scroll and can't think on your feet, your sword's no better than a lump of scrap — dull, clumsy, useless. Face something unexpected, and you'll flail around like a headless chicken.
But it's the name my old man gave me. Maybe he hoped I'd grow up to be some kind of hero. He didn't leave much behind, but carrying this name feels like his sword still leaves its mark on the world.
One day, I was so wiped out I just collapsed. That's when I noticed — not a single drop of sweat beneath his feet. That doddering, clumsy look of his? All an act.

To me, Huaxu is like a clumsy swordsman glued to their Nine Chapters of Dafeng. They can't even deal with a Drifter like me — what chance do they have against a true threat? It's only a matter of time before they fall.
...Ah, it's you. Hello, how are you?

options.content: Got any little secrets you'd like to share with me, Fina?
Did you have a good night's sleep?
Fina, do you have any family other than your brother?

talks.content: Um, I was wondering... if there were a candy that could make me grow very tall...

I have a big glass chest filled with the soft snow from outside my window and marshmallows as white as the snow. I'd also like to put in clouds as fluffy as those marshmallows, and breezes as warm as those clouds...
Mm-hmm! I dreamed of a nightingale, pure as driven snow, resting on my hand one moment, and playing hide-and-seek with me the next... Hmm, was it me who dreamed, or did it dream of me, I wonder?
I used to have a mum and two dads. But they've all gone...
He's the greatest magician, with the most soothing voice and the gentlest soul in the world...
So tall that I could see above the clouds and even touch the stars!
And our giggles and chuckles in there too, every single one~
Perhaps you both visited the same dreamland.
The first dad went to a faraway land with mum. And the second one... he's in that faraway land too... I sent him there.
But what if you accidentally stepped on me and flattened me like a pancake...
Wow... it must be heavenly to nestle inside.

You might be right! Maybe it's a wonderland where all the sleeping children and little animals can play together. Hmm... I wonder who I'll meet in my next dream — Owl the Wise, Miss Canary, or Sir Rabbit?
Er, what's wrong? You look very confused.
I'd walk carefully, I promise! Well... if you're really worried, you could perch on my hand and we'll go for a spin. What do you think?
Well... if you nibble one of those candies that shrinks you down tiny, you could get in for a visit. But everything's white in there, so be careful not to wander off and lose your way.
This is so not the Outsider I know!
If I do get lost in there, will Fina come to find me?
Huh...? You mean he's not kind or gentle to you? I'm so sorry... I'll give him a little tap on his head and ask him to be nicer!
Mmm... If you get lost, I'll scatter breadcrumbs in a trail for you... Follow them and you'll find the way out!
I've been waiting here ever since I woke up. My venom has almost run dry... So, it's a good thing you came. I can feel it bubbling through my veins again. Can you come a little closer...?

options.content: You always seem so happy when it rains.
You're always talking about love. What does "love" really mean to you...?
Your way of thinking is quite special.
Are you alright with that much toxin in your body?
There's always a pleasant smell around you.

talks.content: Yes, I love rainy days. They remind me of the love stories I've read, where romantic encounters always happen on a rainy day.
Ah, you're initiating a conversation about love with me — how unexpected.
Special? Indeed... Many have seen me as a "monster" since I was young.
I'm perfectly fine. My venom is part of me, like a gift from the God of Love — it's harmless to me, and will help me find my destined lover.
It's my signature perfume, with top notes as intense as a first encounter, heart notes of sweet nothings that fix the scent, and a base note that lingers with a bittersweet aftertaste.
Aren't rainy days more for sleeping in? Why would there be romantic encounters?

Hmm, how should I put it? ...It's like water in perfume, which kisses and embraces each ingredient, devours and absorbs their fragrance, and eventually blends with them to create a long-lasting aroma...
The looks of disgust on their faces aren't pleasant, which should be corrected...
Sounds like you really appreciate this gift.
What exactly are the ingredients?
Have you ever observed those seeking shelter from the rain? They meet under eaves, the damp air enhancing the fragrance of greenery, love gently flowing with tentative advances...
You mean it's about cuddling up together every day?
Perhaps a little sting of my toxin in their skin will soften those harsh looks... Hehe.
Of course. Though it often casts me as a monster, it also sets me apart. I believe that the destined lover meant for a monster must be quite special, don't you think?
That's my little secret. However, I'd be delighted to guide you through the blending process myself, one step at a time.
Hehe, join me next time it rains, and you'll see what I mean.

There's much more to that. I seek a love so profound that we become truly inseparable... Even if life itself ends, one will become the mulch for the flowers in our garden; the blooms will turn into perfume, lingering around the other for eternity.
So, when you say "special", do you mean special like a monster... or specially enchanting?
Now's the perfect timing. I should head out before... Huh?! When did you get here?

options.content: You're so quiet today... It's like you're a completely different person.
Thieves are usually quite alert. How do you manage to swipe their stuff right under their noses?
Those who like to steal are no good.
I thought most Charons wouldn't appreciate being called a "demon"...

talks.content: "Berry, I..."
Easy, I can change my look however I want! Hehe, I can take any shape, any colour, and blend in anywhere perfectly. No one can spot me!
Hey! Don't lump me together with those baddies who steal from just anyone! I'm nothing like them!
Of course not. You wouldn't like it either if people called you a "demon" with a frown and disgust.
One time, I even turned into a barrel just to scare you, but you never came near...
How are you any different?
Then why do you call yourself "Demon Tabethe the Red Hand"?
"Your smile in the morning is already the greatest pick-me-up of all. From now on, I'll always be there to keep you safe." Hee hee, pretty convincing, isn't it?
Well, a random barrel popping up in the middle of a room? That's a bit of a giveaway...
I only steal from thieves. I blend in, sneak up close, and pluck my favourite treasures right from their pockets!
That's because I want to make the word "demon" cool. Now, the mere mention of my title "Demon Tabethe the Red Hand" sends shivers down the spine of those thieves.
No! Not even close! And stop mimicking us!
What?! Wait, so you knew it was me and just walked away? That's not cool!
When they find out, their faces are priceless! Hehe... If anything, I'm more like a vigilante!
And one day, the word "demon" will only make people think how awesome I am. That'll be pretty cool, don't you think?
Are you angry? Hehehe, that scowl on your face makes me want to mimic you even more!
One's surroundings shape the spirit, and mindful care strengthens the body. Perhaps a walk beneath these kindly skies would do wonders for your health.

options.content: Is that a medical text you're reading?
Fushu, do you have any dreams?
What's the Hall of Ephemerality like?
As a healer, you must possess a particularly profound understanding of death, don't you?

talks.content: Indeed. Yet, the contents are dense and cryptic, and even the distinctions between certain remedies remain elusive to me. Perhaps I simply lack the aptitude for this craft.
I dream of a world without incurable maladies.
It's a place for healing and saving lives.

Death is like a lamp extinguished — all traces vanish, all voices fade. That isolation, that profound stillness, consumes every glimmer of hope and possibility. If it lies within my power, I would spare any patient from falling into such an abyss.
Really? I thought for a healer, grasping this kind of stuff would be a walk in the park.
That's quite a grand dream...
Can you tell me more about it?
It almost sounds as though you've experienced it firsthand.
In my time... medication was not the primary means of healing. People practised a miraculous healing art called "Zhuyou" to ward off illness.

It rings as but a fanciful daydream, doesn't it? Yet, even without the miracles of healing magic, the purpose of a healer remains unchanged. I must admit, coming from someone who still struggles to fully grasp medical texts, such a speech must sound absurd.

The Hall's mission is singular — to heal, and to heal alone. If one were to speak of other aspects... every healer who trained within its walls planted an apricot tree on the first day of their practice. Yet, as time passed, storms and decay claimed many. Now, fewer than half remain.

You're not mistaken. I... once returned from the brink of death, clawing my way back from the clutches of grave illness. Should such a trial confront me again, I cannot say with certainty that I would make the same choice.

While this method could bring healing and peace, it demanded the sacrifice of a healer's very life force. None of us lived to see old age — pouring out our essence unto death was the only path we knew.
But... I'll continue treading this path — not merely for the sake of others or the legacy of the Hall of Ephemerality, but for my own fulfilment as well.
Waking up from a long slumber, I sought the apricot tree I once planted in my youth. Sadly, the tree had withered to barren wood, and not even this warm spring could coax new buds from its branches.
...That's such a heavy burden to bear.

Life rushes by, like a fleeting horse through a narrow chasm, a spark struck from flint, or a phantom wandering in a dream. How does one find their way back through such transience? The past slips further from reach, while hopes to amend it vanish like morning mist.

The Hall of Ephemerality may now be but a relic of time, yet the path of healing and saving lives has never lacked successors. Even under the heaviest burdens, there will always be those who press forward with unwavering resolve.
Need anything? Spit it out quickly. I've got a mission to finish.

options.content: Can you tell me something about Sibylle?
Heard you pulled quite a few gigs before joining the Legion. Got any pro tips?
You seem to be lost in thought; what's on your mind?
Why do you always push yourself so hard at work?

talks.content: Sibylle? She's the chief of the 13th Legion.
Tips? The only tip I have is there's no problem a good punch can't fix. If that doesn't work, throw another.
Saw a really nice gun the other day... Forget it, can't skimp on food just to buy it. The old one feels better in my hands anyway.
No work, no food. What don't you get?
Anything else?
What if two punches don't sort it out either?
If you really like it, maybe I can get one for you.
But it's also important to find a balance, right?
Ugh, what do you expect me to know? She calls the shots, I do the work. That's all.
Then a bullet usually does the trick.
Really?... Nah, you look as broke as me... I appreciate the gesture, but don't go break a piggy bank for me. I don't wanna owe anyone anything.
Balance would be great, but my clients don't see it that way — always hounding me, "Is the job done yet? Hurry up!" Ugh, if I didn't have a family to feed, I'd punch them in their stupid faces.
But I heard some people can take a bullet and still stand.
It's just a figure of speech. My point is: be as tough and strong as you can be, and that's all you need. Keep nitpicking, and your face will be getting those punches next.
Yale: Hi... Such a nice day, isn't it... Perfect for some explosive experiments... Um, what a nice day.

options.content: Are you interested in Phoxhunter commissions? Care to join me?
You seem to always speak very slowly.
Were you and Oliver childhood friends?

talks.content: Yale: Oliver is not a talking bomb... It might sound strange, but... he's actually...
Yale: I... I might not be much help. The only thing I'm good at... is probably making Tot Poppers...
Yale: Ah, sorry! B-But if I start speaking fast, my tongue tends to get all t-t-tied up.
Yale: I never really had a "childhood"... From my earliest memories, I've been in this body. Oliver might have one, though.
Oliver: Ugh, you're killing me here! I am Yale, and Yale is me. Got it? Not that I'd expect someone with your pea-sized brain to understand.
Hmm? What's a Tot Popper?
It must be hard for you to communicate with others then.
Missing out on childhood, that's kind of sad.
What a rude bomb, maybe you should get rid of it.
Yale: They're the most popular items at our "Snap 'n' Spark" toy store... They take a lot of time to make.
Yale: I-It's okay, sometimes Oliver speaks for me... And when no one else's around, Oliver would always hear me out.
Yale: I've sometimes wondered what having a "childhood" would be like... Would Mr Jones have told me bedtime stories every night, like a normal dad...?
Yale: Oliver's a-a-actually a nice guy! He might s-seem a bit rough, and mean, a-and likes to pop up out of the b-blue, but...
Yale: But it's not because I'm skilled... It's all thanks to Oliver's expertise.
Oliver: You expect that jerk to tell you bedtime stories? Have you lost your mind?
Oliver: Hey! That's your idea of nice words?
Yale: S-Sorry! I-I know he only cared about his experiments... He wouldn't have done that...
Ready for the interrogation?

options.content: Your skin is as red as fire. That's quite unique.
Why did you choose to become a warden?
Is being a warden a busy job?
What does justice mean to you?
What do you do in your spare time?

talks.content: If you learned about history, you'd know that the first warden of the Royal Military Prison had skin like molten lava. Even the most ruthless criminals feared her interrogations.
Since the Empire's inception, my family has managed the prison that holds the most heinous criminals, correcting wrongs and neutralising threats.
Certainly. The Imperial Prison is teeming with devious criminals. My duties include conducting interrogations, reviewing case files, and thwarting escape attempts.
Justice? It is the restraint of desire through power, the suppression of evil through strength, and the punishment of the wicked by the mighty.
With criminals still roaming the streets of the Empire, spare time is a luxury for a warden. The only respite I get is when I sneak in a few strong drinks amidst a busy schedule.
As her descendant, I proudly bear her name, ready to incinerate all sins with my fire.

My fiery red skin, a legacy from the first warden, predestined me to continue enforcing the iron-clad code she established. So it wasn't me who chose to become a warden; it was the mantle of warden that chose me.
Every minute of rest delays justice a bit, and when justice is delayed, chaos and the law of the jungle take over.
Isn't that a bit "painting with a broad brush"?
What!? You drink!?
Then... does your scorching skin make everyday life difficult?
Does that mean you've already achieved your aspirations?
Would your job be easier if there were fewer prisoners?

Hmph, broad? I wouldn't expect a naive child to understand. We don't live in a utopia where people simply hold hands and love each other. Only through absolute power and order can true justice be secured!

Why so surprised? It's merely a diversion. During interrogations, I always hear about various kinds of alcohol, which made me curious about this so-called wicked potion that seems to be associated with crime. So I drink once in a while.

It does pose some challenges — I can only sleep on iron beds and can't linger in wooden structures for long. However, it allows me to pull criminals from burning buildings and administer justice. And the cold never bothers me.
Becoming a warden is merely the beginning. It compels me to remain vigilant, eradicating any injustice within the Empire until my final breath.
Some scholars have envisioned a crime-free world. Should such a day come, my purpose would vanish, for evil necessitates a warden's existence. Until then, I am committed to upholding order.
And the more I drink, the more I'm convinced that it's not the drink that is wicked.
My unusual appearance is more of a gift. If there's any downside... I've always wanted to try ice cream, but it melts in my hand before I can taste it...
I've cleared the snow from your doorstep on my way here! Touched, huh? Bet you're thinking of treating me to a cup of cocoa~

options.content: "The One-Stop Rubbish Bin Map Guide of Icelake"...?
I sometimes see you gazing at the distant snowfields. Do you wish to leave here?
What animal is on your charm?
You know, people in the slums call you "Princess Rubbish Bin".

talks.content: Well... it's about giving discarded items a new home and providing those in need with a chance at a better life.
Shhhh! That's a scavenger's top secret! I wouldn't have let you in on it if you hadn't helped me out with that thief!
Oh, you've got it backwards! I love Icelake through and through. It's just that I often reminisce about the days I spent wandering the snowfields with my dad; that's how I grew up.

That's the big cat that used to roam the snowfields with me when I was little! We called him "Plumpytail". He would only let me pet him in exchange for some jerky, but oh, the feel of his fur — hehehe, it's the best of the best!
Nah-uh! That's not me! I'm too grown up for such a childish title! Please, I beg of you, don't ever call me that again!
And how's that done?
This map charts every rubbish bin in Icelake, and I've marked the few where the best stuff tends to gather — I've upgraded those bins to larger sizes and timed my visits to perfection!
How do you feel about those days?
What does a big snowfield cat sound like? More like a cat or a tiger?
Then how would you like to be referred to?

For instance, turning an aristocrat's cast-off velvet curtains into warm winter coats for the elderly, or bringing discarded dolls to children whose only playthings are pebbles — they'll be overjoyed for a long time.
But scavenging is really hit-or-miss — mostly, it all comes down to luck...

From here, the snowfields look like something out of a fairy tale. But once you step into it, you'd feel so very small. Even after trudging through knee-high snow for hours, that feeling would never leave.
Mmm... it's certainly not like "meow"; it's more like, "raawr—raawr—!"
Ahem, that would be — Lady Margie the reticent detective, a lone shadow-walker of the city! Today, I will unveil for you the secrets of Icelake, as always!

There was one time, I dragged back a broken bookshelf someone had thrown out. Though I was half-dead from the effort, it quickly turned into a non-stop playground for a litter of kittens — totally worth it!
Scavenging's no picnic, that's for sure...
I don't hate those days. But the bustling, lively Icelake is my absolute favourite!
Is Plumpytail still around?
Hehe, now that's a proper title for me~
That's scavenging for you! It's mostly small fry stuff, but never a dull moment. So, what do you say, wanna join us?
Ha, I knew you'd understand!
Plumpytail prefers the wild over city life. We had to go our separate ways, but she'll always be a part of me, just like the snowfields.
Patrol complete. No signs of dangerous creatures, structural damage, or suspicious markings. Routine operations may proceed without interruption. Report concluded.

options.content: It seems like you really like playing the harmonica.
How's life in the Legion treating you?
You seem to have a stronger sense of responsibility than your fellow soldiers when carrying out missions.
I just cleaned the mirrors at the base. Want to take a look?
Do you still have your harmonica with you?
How are you managing lately? Are you doing okay financially?
How have you been holding up since leaving the Legion?

talks.content: Oh... You've noticed. Yes, I have one — it was given to me by someone very dear. I keep it locked away safely, but... I can't help checking on it now and then, worried it might just vanish somehow.

Not bad. The Legion is one of the few places where hard work truly gets rewarded. I've earned my position here, and now I even have a few subordinates. I make sure they treat Charons and Solas with the same respect.
I wouldn't call it responsibility. I'm simply following the Escort's regulations to the letter.
No... Thank you. I don't really enjoy looking at myself in the mirror. Seeing my horns always makes me feel... uncomfortable.
I do... but it feels so heavy now, almost unbearably so. I'm not sure I have the strength to pick it up and play anymore.
I've been taking on odd jobs here and there. It's enough to cover my expenses. But honestly, earning a living isn't the point anymore. These days, work is more about keeping myself busy.

Better than if I'd stayed, I suppose. The Legion was once my refuge, the place where I thought my dreams could take flight. But those dreams... they turned out to be illusions, and that so-called refuge was a hell that dragged my loved one into an unending abyss of despair...
Then you must know how to play lots of tunes on it.

I've heard plenty of complaints — and bitter accusations — about how harshly the Legion treats the Charon community. I do everything I can to change that... Maybe someday, people will start to see the Legion in a better light.
But the other soldiers don't seem to do the same — they're always so reckless and rude.
So, you're not comfortable with how Charons look?
After all, it once carried all my hopes and dreams. Now, it just reminds me of everything I've lost.
Keeping busy?
Now, my heart burns with the desire for vengeance, yet I can't bring myself to aim my weapon at those I once called comrades. I feel lost... Tell me, what should I do?
Actually, I only know one. The person who gave it to me taught me. I wasn't quick to pick it up back then... maybe because I've never been good at things that require emotional expression...
But are there enough people like you to really make a difference?
The Escort's regulations forbid any legionary from commenting on the conduct of their fellow legionaries.

No, that's not it at all. I'm not ashamed of my Charon heritage. It's just... I think my horns would look much better if they were more regular, more symmetrical. Ah, don't get me wrong! I'm not saying there's anything wrong with your horn...
If you ever feel ready to play it again, I'd be honoured to be your first listener.
Yes... Work gives me purpose. It makes me happy. When I'm busy, even the sunlight feels a little warmer.
I think that's a question only you can answer.
But whenever I'm too tense or carried away, I find myself reaching for it. It's like an anchor — a reminder of the things that matter, the things I can trust. It always helps me find my calm again.

Not yet. But there will be. There was a time when you wouldn't find even a single Charon in the Legion. I know I can't make a big difference just yet, but if I guide my subordinates down the right path, I believe the conflicts between Charons and Solas will ease, bit by bit.
That said, I really don't understand them. Maybe, to them, it's just a job. As long as their superiors don't notice, they think it's fine to slack off or mess around.
...Thank you. I promise, when the day comes that I can pick it up again — when I'm ready to learn a new tune — I'll make sure you're the first to hear it.
...Sorry, I lost my cool. You're right — I need to figure it out on my own, instead of placing that weight on you. Though... it might take me some time.
Many of my peers rely on doctors for stress relief — sedatives, stimulants, that kind of stuff. I've never needed that. Whether my heart races or slows, the harmonica always steadies me.

Treating everyone fairly and keeping them safe from Filthoids and Deterioration... I believe these efforts can improve life for the Charon community. Maybe, it will quiet the weary sighs echoing through Icelake a little bit.

I think that kind of attitude is wrong. People need something to keep themselves in check. Without it, they'll just drift through life, letting their standards erode little by little — until they're no better than rats in the sewers.
Ah, so you've come to see me... Are you still resentful? Conflicted, perhaps? Or have you become indifferent toward me? It makes no difference. We have all the time in the world to figure it out.

options.content: For a merchant, is everything a potential trade?
Do you have any tips for doing business?
What do you do in your leisure time?
I noticed you seem to be afraid of the dark.

talks.content: There is nothing that cannot be leveraged in a negotiation. The only question is — what price will move the scales in your favour?

Mmm... Never lose yourself in fleeting profits and losses. Play the long game. Be generous when needed. Learn to read people, to use them, and to grant them favours, so that they respect you, admire you, and also fear you. True power lies in that delicate balance.
I am often entangled in the minutiae of business, rarely afforded the luxury of leisure.
Hmm? So, you've noticed. An old habit, nothing more.
Even when the price is your life?
That's not quite what I had in mind.

Yet, if fate were to grant me a fleeting moment of respite... I would likely seek solace in the theatre. Be it the age-old storytelling traditions of Huaxu, the refined operas of the Empire, or the avant-garde films gaining traction overseas — each offers its own intrigue.
When I was little, an accident left me stranded in a pitch-black ravine for three days and nights. It was then that this... tendency took root.
Indeed. Your life, mine, and the lives of countless others — each is but a piece on a grander board, their worth determined only by the stakes at play.

Heh. Goods have fixed prices, but human connections are a different currency altogether. Those who haggle over every coin will remain forever bound to their little corner of the market. Only by mastering the art of influence can one rise above mere trade and ascend to true greatness.
It seems our meeting at the theatre wasn't just a coincidence, then.
In this world, everyone harbours their own fears. I am no exception... You seem surprised. May I ask why?
For those as insignificant as we, to exchange what little we have for what we desire... is that not, in itself, a stroke of fortune?

Heh... No, I suppose not. Theatre distils fleeting moments of life, yet within those fragments, it unveils profound truths about the human soul — one that defies reason, thrives in contradiction, and remains endlessly captivating in its unpredictability.
I just thought... you don't seem like someone who has fears or weaknesses.
Does my answer unsettle you? Then, by all means, prove me wrong.
So, what unexpected turns will you bring to my story? I shall be watching with keen interest.
Heh... You're right. Weakness can be a merchant's undoing.
I underwent rigorous training to suppress this fear. At the negotiating table, I can cast it aside with ease. But in your presence, there is no need for such pretences.
Do what you need to. Cherish your freedom before the chains of law bind you.

options.content: You said you're from Huaxu. What is the place like?
You call yourself a servant guarding the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. What does that mean?
You always seem so sombre. Has something happened recently?
I notice you often gaze at the moon at night.

talks.content: ...Go read a tome or seek another's company for such trivial discourse. Perhaps the Starweavers peddling their crafts would indulge your curiosity.
The Nine Chapters are the sacred laws of Huaxu, brooking no defiance. Should anyone dare to challenge divine decree, it falls upon some to quell the ensuing turmoil.
There is nought to celebrate. That is the entirety of the matter.
Indeed. The moon, a celestial marvel, purifies the remnants of the day, be it festivity or foul deed. Through the ages, the crescent merely watches from its lofty perch.
Everyone looks at the world differently. I'm asking about your views.
Does that make you a respected senior official then?
Maybe you can try sharing your troubles with me.
Are you thinking about the past?
I am often preoccupied, and my perspectives are notably skewed. Should your curiosity truly beckon, a visit thither would enlighten you far beyond any second-hand account.
...Perhaps in title. I seldom consort with the commoners. My presence, necessary as it may be for law's enforcement, often brings collateral grief. Few in Huaxu would greet me with joy.
Your concern is appreciated, yet I would not burden another soul with my woes. It is unnecessary.
No, I am one who has bid farewell to the past. Tonight, I simply indulged in an extra half cup of wine.
Ahh... I feel so fresh after just waking up. Listen, buddy, there's no point in working all day. Your to-do list will never end. Remember, relaxation is a necessity, not a luxury.

options.content: Have you always been this idle? Doesn't your family say anything about this?
How come you nap just about anywhere?
What's it like working under Chief Sibylle?

talks.content: My family? My parents haven't really fussed over me for years; just my sisters occasionally trying to boss me around. But now that I'm in the Legion, they're out of reach.

Huh, you're one of those who don't appreciate a good rest! Listen up: Beds are havens, where souls find ease; rooftops sanctuaries, where anxieties cease. In afternoon gardens, the sunlight gleams; take a nap, and enjoy the symphony of sweet dreams...
She sure knows how to run you ragged... I'd need to split myself in three just to keep up... Ahem, I mean, Chief Sibylle is always perfectly strict with us.
I've rigged up something awesome for you — a tiny robot sidekick! It'll follow you around in battle, waving a little banner and cheering, "Go get'em! You're smashing it!"
Sounds like your sisters are pretty mean.
(Turn around and leave)
Too late, I heard that clearly.
Pretty cool, huh? Just wait till I actually get it working...
Oh, not at all! T-They're absolutely delightful, smart, kind-hearted, gentle, charming, beautiful, and just about perfect! Though, a bit more decorum would be nice...
...Hey! I wasn't done!
...How about I treat you to some afternoon tea, and we pretend this conversation never happened? Don't worry, it won't be spiked.
(Turn around and leave)
Hey, I didn't finish! I drew up these plans during my precious breaks — do you know how hard it was for me to keep them from Chief Sibylle?
Watching your relentless efforts to strengthen yourself, I can't help but look forward to the day you challenge me again.

options.content: As a Charon, why would you still serve the Empire?
Have you ever thought about how you'd feel if someone took your family the way you've taken others'?
Given the Empire's disdain for Charons, I imagine they don't look kindly on you either.

talks.content: A special force under the direct command of the Emperor, tasked with covert missions and serving as a hammer ready to strike on the battlefield.
Hmph, my allegiance is not to the Empire, but to my ideals. A man once gave everything for these, and it is his legacy that I strive to uphold.
It's okay. My family's long gone anyway.
Indeed. I've endured my share of curses and jibes to my face, and those from the gutter surely grumble even more.
Huh, backed by the Emperor — no wonder you're always so overbearing.
You're just making excuses. No matter the reason, your actions are nothing more than enabling tyranny.
Fortunately, in this unjust world, absolute power can still earn one a modicum of respect.
You got it all wrong. Without the Emperor, the Legion still stands; without the Legion, however, the crown would surely fall.

You're not wrong. To get what I desire, I'll use everything at my disposal and climb the ladder by any means necessary; but each step I take is a step closer to what I believe in. Where have your steps led you?
I find it liberating, actually. It means no more distractions — just a clear path to contend with my enemies, both known and hidden.
In that case, if you ever lost your power, they'd certainly kick you hard while you're down.
Should I report you for treason based on that statement?
Sentiment and feelings are merely weaknesses for anyone in the Legion.
Exactly, which is why I'll never show weakness; otherwise, they'd pounce like wolves at the scent of blood, eager to tear me apart.
Feel free to try. Treason is a grave offence, and any accusation would work its way up through the ranks and end up right on my desk.
The sun is shining bright, and the little birdies are chirping with joy after a hearty meal. Are you hungry too? Wanna grab something to eat as well?

options.content: I heard you're a commissary. What's that all about?
Just wondering — does it hurt to get bumped by Filbert?
Filbert's so cute. She must be a good helper.
I've been meaning to say — your dress is really cute.
You seem to have been zoning out here for a while.

talks.content: Huh? You don't know? A commissary's job is to make sure everyone's well-fed, dealing with all sorts of food every day.
Hmm... maybe it does? I've never really thought about it, but Filbert only knocks down those no-good, shouty, fighty troublemakers! They totally deserve it!
Yeah, she is! And you know what, even across several creeks, Filbert can sniff out ripe berries and then off we go charging! Pretty awesome, isn't she?
Thank you! Actually, these are shorts, not a dress. They did start as a pretty, long, white dress; then the lady at the tailor's shop turned them into shorts for me.
Oh, I was meditating, not zoning out. I'm a member of the Elysian Church after all, so I do try to give some deep thought occasionally.
For example, I go out to gather all kinds of ingredients from the wild, have Filbert haul them back, and then get Mr Beard at the bakery to turn them into yummy food for everyone.
Those guys always end up hungry after their brawls. They'd do more good ploughing fields than swinging weapons — that way, less people would go to bed hungry.
Awesome. No risk of food shortage then.
Why is that?
What were you thinking, then? Why isn't there a god of full bellies, perhaps?
And just so you know, haggling with Mr Beard is part of my job too! Hehe.
You must really hate wars, then.
No worries at all! Filbert always brings more food. So never ever make fun of her — it would hurt her feelings, and mine too.
Because dresses aren't the best for all the running around I do. One time, I tripped over the hem and all the bread in my arms went flying.
I used to wonder about that, but the clergy said it was... blastphomy or something. So I stopped thinking about that.
Wow! That sounds impressive. Is it the same for all commissaries?
Absolutely! Fighting just leads to hunger — that's really awful! I've heard that in times of war, everyone ends up starving, which is just the worst! I hope I never have to see that.
But if the day comes, when no one's starving anymore, I'll have them changed back into a dress!
I never quite get what they say, like how gluttony is a terrible sin... but it seems like the higher someone's status, the more they eat.
Oh, not at all! The others seem to be brainy types; they're all about the paperwork — filling out application forms, then waiting for trains loaded with food to roll in.
If war does break out, you could mount Filbert and ram those troublemakers.
But for a small town like ours, just Filbert and I can feed everyone! Otherwise, I might have to start filling out those forms too — ugh, it's all gibberish to me.
Right! Anyone who makes people go hungry will sooner or later get knocked over by Filbert!
Here you are, finally! I've finished all my chores and got absolutely knackered, but I've only earned a few quid. Urgh... You know I do much for you guys.

options.content: Do you have something like a quickstart guide to becoming a seasoned Phoxhunter to share?
Why is the Empire making such a big deal about "The Forsakens"? What are they?
What is that thing in your hand?!

talks.content: A guide? No, most folks in this trade aren't the type to stick their nose in a book. But I do have a few mottoes to share, like my personal fighting mantra: "Two hits in the ribs, one on the head; so dead even the emperor can't pull 'em back."
They're like a wildfire that's never fully extinguished, ready to flare up at any moment. For your own good, better keep your distance...
Yeah. Can you grab that bandage over there for me? I need to keep it from Fina, or she'll make a big fuss again.
Oh, would you like some? Don't mind their looks — just pop off the head, and they're crunchy like cookies, even with a hint of meaty aftertaste...
Wait a sec, why do you only have a few coins in your hand? Did you give away your share of the bounty again?
Interesting, got any more?
Why? What's it to me?
She's just concerned about you.
(Turn around and run)
They needed the money more than I did.
Don't bite off more than you can chew. In our line of work, greed is the biggest enemy — sometimes it comes from others, but more often, it comes from within.
Well... let's just say we've had our little scuffles. If you ever deal with them, make sure my name doesn't come up.
I know, but injuries are part of the job. I'd rather she not worry so much. Cover for me if she asks, will you? I owe you one.
Wha... where are you going!? This is vital survival wisdom... If you got lost in the wild with no food, these little critters could be a lifesaver.
But... Never mind, this is you, always looking out for others. Let me know if you're ever short on cash.
Actually, I'm short right now.
...You're milking it, buddy.
Such a relief — I'm still here today. And so are you...

options.content: That's really a lovely dress, but are you not worried about catching a cold?
I remember you mentioned that people don't look kindly on Charons in Hyperborea.
There's a flowery smell around here lately.
Have you ever left Icelake, Psyche?
It seems like you have something on your mind.

talks.content: Thank you! Actually, we Charons are quite resilient to the cold, so there's no need for expensive, heavy coats.
Yeah, it's been that way for ages. We're treated like pests and I've faced harassment and insults for no reason.
Ah, that might be from my new gardening project. The courtyard at the Hypnos' House looked a bit barren with just a few trees, so I planted some white flowers there.
No, I've been here my whole life. I always hear those trains and wonder about the places they're heading to. I'd really love to see what's out there.
Oh, it's just that... I want to take a good look at you all, to memorize your faces better.
My mom made this dress, but I chose the colour — this vibrant green — and the butterfly details too. They'd look right at home somewhere warm, like the south.
Is it because Solas fear what Charons can do?
Perhaps we should plant some here too — bellflowers, windflowers, white dryas... Which would suit this place best?
What places are on your wish list?
Could you maybe take a moment to look at me carefully? I'd like you to remember me... just as I am right now.
I see. The butterflies are a nice touch — they suit you perfectly.
Probably. They say "Magic is the root of all evil." History books claim our ancestors used it to rule over Solas more than a thousand years ago, committing terrible acts.
Maybe you could ask around and gather everyone's thoughts on it.

Mm, I'd definitely want to visit the capital, for starters; Uncle Henrik once told me the sunsets in Scarletriver are breathtaking... Oh, and I'd love to visit Purgatorio Island you told me about — to feel the sea breeze and see if it's as salty as you described!
Really? That's so nice to hear! Actually, I've only seen blue butterflies around Icelake. I'd love to see what other colours are out there someday.
Honestly, I can hardly imagine that... The Charons I know are too terrified of Solas to even speak up around them, let alone use magic.
Right, it should be a group decision... I'll ask around! By the way, which flower do you like best? I'll pick some for you when they bloom.
And Most Charon magic is quite ordinary — just good for simple things like lighting fireplaces or freezing food.
Would you wish to go back to those times — when Charons ruled over Solas?
Not at all. Why must one rule over the other? Why can't Charons and Solas just live in peace?
All I wish for is that when spring comes, everyone can go out together to enjoy all kinds of flowers. That would be enough for me.
It's delightful to see you safe and well today. Take care... The peace we all long for will surely arrive someday.

options.content: What do you like to do in your downtime away from the battlefield?
Could you tell me about alchemy?
I've noticed you always carry that backpack. What do you keep inside?
Training as a medic must be tough, isn't it?
Sometimes I see you staring at your radio.

talks.content: I... don't think I have any particular hobbies. Reading, maybe, if that counts.
Certainly! Alchemy is the cornerstone of Hyperborea — scholars call it the "primordial miracle."
Some emergency tools and supplies — bandages, antiseptics, anesthetics, and the basic tools for wound care like surgical blades and sutures.
Oh, it's fine! I can handle it... Well, maybe just a little tough sometimes. The emergency care and nursing lessons aren't too bad, but the physical fitness tests... those are a real struggle for me.
...The last time I spoke with my father was over the radio. It was on the battlefield of Lonza Fortress, and despite the danger, he told me, "Don't worry, I'll be fine."
My mother always says staying home with my books and skipping all those balls and salons will cost me countless opportunities to climb the social ladder...
At first, its purpose was simple: to extract gold from Phoxene. But over time, we discovered this tiny crystal could do so much more — power machinery, generate electricity... It's Solarian magic.
I also keep a handkerchief and a comb in it.

Even though I get up earlier than everyone else for extra training, I still only manage to scrape by with passing scores... Please don't make fun of me! Building stamina is so much harder than studying.
After everything that happened, I'd often turn on my radio in the dead of night, tune to his channel, and press the call button, hoping to hear his voice again...
But honestly, I prefer it this way.
...But then, the Academy...
You bring beauty supplies to the battlefield? You must take great care in staying elegant.
Waking up early for extra training sounds exhausting.
It wasn't until I sat there in silence for what felt like an eternity that I realized... he was never coming back.
What are you reading these days?
You used to study there, didn't you?
Oh, it's not what you think... They're not for me — they're for my patients. I use them to help those who don't make it... tidy up a bit.

It is. But when I take my mind off my tired legs and look up, I see the wheat fields stretching beyond the city and the cottages on the horizon, and hear the windmills creaking and the herdsmen whistling. It always helps me feel so much better.
My condolences...
Mostly books on battlefield medicine — Emergency Field Aid Manual, Practical Guide to Trauma Care, How to Set Up a Temporary Field Hospital...
...Yes, in the Spathatoi. But that chapter of my life is over now.
The cruelty of death robs people of more than just their lives — it strips them of their dignity.
Because... running along that road feels like my way of protecting these simple, precious things from being taken away.
Thank you. Don't worry, I'll stay strong and keep pushing on. Until I clear my father's name and honour the wronged who fell in the Lonza battle, I won't stop.
You may know that my previous studies never focused on first aid, so even with my medic qualifications, I still feel out of my depth sometimes.
Why did you leave?

I just want... when their families come to say their final goodbyes, for them to see their loved ones at peace, as though they're merely asleep. After being apart for so long, no parent should have to see their child's face twisted in pain...
You should try to unwind now and then. Don't push yourself too hard.

I left because the Spathatoi lost its way. What began as a pursuit of knowledge turned into something darker. It's become the blazing core of Hyperborea's war machine, but its fuel brings suffering and misfortune to its people.
I know, which is why I've been reading... Glass Heels. It's about a—a princess and a knight... Not that I'm into romantic novels or anything! I just... happened to flip through it, that's all...
I suppose... I wasn't as strong as I thought. I couldn't reconcile with what it had become, and I lacked the courage or strength to change it. So, I did the only thing I could — I walked away.
Whatever they demand of us... remember this: we are not monsters.
I asked the doctor for a pen and some paper — could you fetch the seal for me? Apologies... this injury's turned me into a burden.
Please be careful. I'll be waiting for you right here.
When did you get injured?
During the attack by that giant Filthoid. I didn't mean to hide it from you, but...
...You need a break. Listen to Sir Avar and go to the processing area.
I'll go see you when we're back in the capital.
Okay. After what Commander Avar said, I guess I don't have a choice. But I'm still worried...
Forget it. Now that he's here, there shouldn't be any problems.

name: Temporary Pushcart Mechanism (Do Not Talk to It)

talks.content: <W>That's right — you've made the right choice. Grip the hilt tightly. Yes, just like that. Now aim at the creature's throat...</>
{nickname2}...My god, what have you done!?
<W>That's right! Forget about meaningless reason. Just follow my lead...</>
It was the sound of passing time, the roar of life that once was, the heartbeat of an embryo, and an ancient echo sealed deeply within my heart.
I felt as though I had become one with this primal voice.
Plop... Plop... Plop...
AARGH...!
What's gotten into you? You scared me!
(Were those just... an illusion...?)
...Leon, keep a close watch on her. Bring her back in one piece, and make sure she doesn't harm herself. Use Frank as leverage if necessary.
Yes, sir!
Wait!
Remember what I said back on our way to the turret? "Your kindness will reap a just reward."
Lend me your ear. I've got a secret that's just for you. Rest assured, you've just frisked me. I am really out of weapons.
It may be extremely important to you. You sure you don't want to hear it?
<W>Someone in your Legion wants you dead.</>
Leon, shut her up.
What did you say?
Hehe, fine. I hope you won't regret your choice.
Secrets are meant to be whispered once. Take care, sir.

Ah, it's you... Let me know if you need to buy a ticket.
Did you find anything?

options.content: Have you been wandering around here all this time? Is there anything I can help you with?

talks.content: I... I feel so foggy. Honestly, I don't even know who I am — or where this place is.
A kind-hearted doctor found me up in the northern mountains and brought me back. She said I had a terrible fever... and that it probably damaged my memory.

options.content: I understand. Losing a sense of belonging is awful.
Staying out here isn't safe. It's best to figure out your true identity as soon as possible.
Seeing is not always believing. You've got to investigate everything thoroughly before jumping to conclusions.

talks.content: The only thing I could remember these past few days was the relentless blizzard as I struggled to make my way across the mountain... But right now I'm in no condition to go anywhere. Could you help me with the investigation?
Apart from the kind doctor who saved me, you are the only one willing to offer a helping hand to a penniless girl like me. I don't know what else to say but thank you...
Oh — this was in my coat pocket. I don't remember anything about it... but maybe it's important?

(The threads begin to connect between the two individuals you've recently come across — Ms Elsa, who's been driven near to madness in search of her daughter, and this amnesiac girl. And then there's the letter, seemingly penned to a mother.)
(The thought crosses your mind that the girl bereft of memory might very well be Elsa's missing daughter, Annie.)

(Intuition suggests bringing her to Elsa for recognition, yet Elsa's delusion leads her to see Annie in every youthful face... Gathering more substantial evidence of the girl's identity seems the prudent course at the moment.)
(If anyone holds the key to this girl's past, it's the doctor who saved her back then.)
Ladies and gentlemen, drop by and drop a few coins, and you can join The Fisheries in Icelake to get the best and latest— Oh! It's you...
Is this yours?
Ah! That's it! The book I used to pore over for hours as a kid. I'd sit there staring at the pictures, dreaming of life beyond our tiny island...
Thank you. Thank you so much. I need to give it a good read tonight. But for now, *sigh* making a living is more important.
Take care. And no more scamming people, alright? Oh, and here — some dried fish, caught off Purgatorio Island.
Oh, wow... Thank you. Really. Thank you so much...

Ladies and gentlemen, those who are interested in Icelake Fishermen's Mutual Aid Society can learn more about it. We have decades of fishing experience from veteran fishermen. Fishing is great either serving as a hobby or a job!
Ah, {Nickname}! Great to see you again! Us old island folk ought to swap fishing tricks sometime, eh?
Maybe next time.
It was so hard to leave when I was young, and now I can't go back...
Take care.
Beat it, dirty Charon!
(Dressed in ragged military garb, the Charon man before you sends menacing glares towards the passersby.)

options.content: (He seems temperamental. Maybe touching his horns will calm him down.)
Charons and Solas are equals. Prejudice is not cool.
But you're a Charon too... aren't you?

talks.content: Oi! What are you doing?! Looking for trouble?!
Look at that, a saint here! Why not enlighten the security bureau with your little sermon? Maybe they'll reward you with a free lesson on how to watch your mouth.
How dare you! Who do you think you're talking to? You think you and I are the same kind?
You've got horns too, just like us.
Think the security bureau would show you any respect if you were in my shoes?
For your information, we Charons aren't all cut from the same cloth!
Since I was a kid, I've held myself to Sola standards, and never mingled with other Charons. Ever met a Charon who speaks like I do? Just so you know, this is a standard Dismania accent!
My Sola friends all say they can't tell that I'm actually a Charon from the way I speak. They say I sound just like one of them.
Jealous, huh? Well, I've earned this!
For three years straight, I'd start every morning reading "Hyperborean News" for two hours, fine-tuning my accent while cringing at the crimes some Charon had disgracefully committed.
Got it? I'm more Sola than any of you could ever be, that's why I've become an officer, while you roam around in rags like a beggar.
Alright, I've indulged you this long only because my heart's as big as any Sola's. Consider this as a gratis lesson for you Charons. Now shoo, take your lowlife vibes away from me.

options.content: May I have the honour to take a peek at your "Laurelled Charon" medal?

talks.content: Huh? What did you say?
I've heard about this "Laurelled Charon" medal that Hyperborea grants to the most distinguished Charons.
Someone as brave, loyal, and with an impeccable accent like you must have one. I'd be thrilled to finally see it!
...I... must've left it at home! Maybe next time!
Is that so? I truly admire you, sir!
I've heard that Laurelled Charons are entitled to live in the inner city. You must own a splendid mansion there, like something out of a storybook — with legions of butlers and servants!
Of course!
There's that famous "Maidé Upp" fountain in the inner city, isn't there?
A lowly Charon like me will probably never get to see it. Could you tell me if the statue by the fountain is a lion or a wolf. Please, sir, I'm dying to be enlightened!
Err... it's... a lion. Right, a lion!
Are you sure, sir? Because a friend of mine said...
Ah, wait... had a rough night, headache's killing me! Now that I think about it, it's a wolf — walked by it just this morning, happy now?
(A veneer of admiration remains on your face, yet a whirlwind of emotions sweeps through your mind — from initial anger to bewilderment, settling finally on pity.)
Seems your memory's still playing tricks on you. Because there's no "Maidé Upp" fountain — it's actually a made-up fountain.
You crafty little twerp...! How dare you—!
(Anticipating his move, you nimbly dodged the man's furious punch.)
Goodbye, sir. Hope I can pick your brain about the inner city again some other time.
Scram!! Don't let me catch sight of you again!! Beat it!!!
Mist Aken's got no entertainment at all... There's gotta be an untapped market hiding somewhere. I'll figure something out... sooner or later...
True to my passion for knowledge, true to... Ugh, what exactly does it mean to say stay true to it?
I am just an archaeologist! Passion has nothing to do with my studies!

options.content: Passion is the will to unravel what you really want.
Passion is the force that sustains life itself.
Passion is the unspoken that hides from the light of day.

talks.content: I don't even know what I really want...
Such depth — too vast for me to grasp...
Oh, I see! No wonder I didn't get it.
That's an interesting take. Can you help me get what passion really means?
I am a researcher with the Imperial Branch of Archaeological Society of Atlasia. Lately, the research reports I've submitted keeps being returned with the same remark — no passion can be felt within.
Ugh... I just don't get what the investor want...
An investor who understands research? Since when does that happen?

Mr Qiu isn't just some investor. He is the investor who uncovered the century-sunken ships in the Republic of Luca, the ruins in Elysium buried for thousands of years, and the battlefield in Hyperborea lost to time. Each stands a milestone in the annals of archaeology.
