Mr Qiu is the chief investor of Archaeological Society, as well as a renowned archaeologist and collector. Whispers persist that he is none other than a sovereign who walks within the "shadow" of Huaxu.
If it weren't for his backing, the Archaeological Society wouldn't have developed into such a a huge organization spreading across the continent today.
Ugh... He never really cared before, so why's he suddenly clinging to us now? Is life in retirement truly so idle in Huaxu?
Can I read your research reports?

Of course! A Brief Analysis of the Customer Flow in Icelake's Taverns, The Craft and Evolution of Drink-Brewing in Asphodel, or Observational Records of the Luno Naming Itself the Demon King. Which one would you like to read?

options.content: For an academic report, it doesn't really sound that academic.
Tell me... Has any of your work to do with true archaeology?

talks.content: Well, what choice have I? Nothing lies beneath the snow of Icelake. Then how am I supposed to write a proper archaeology report?

options.content: That's it — you see nothing up top and give up right away. No wonder the investor said he can't feel any passion.

talks.content: It's not like I want it this way! Passion, what is it? I am sure haven't found it here in Icelake.

options.content: Perhaps you need a proper guide.

talks.content: I can't find one. Phoxhunters here only care about fights and drinks. I once asked if there were any historic ruins nearby, only to be asked back whether their stewpots counted as relics.
How about.... you take me around and see if we can find some inspiration. Of all the regulars at the Asphodel, you looks like the one who drinks the least and reads the most.

options.content: Alright, let's see if we can dig up some inspiration for you.
Pay up, and I'll help you brainstorm.
You came to the right person — I am the top-notch intellectual. Now share some of your research funding with me and I shall help you.

talks.content: Please don't give up on me!
Achoo! It's getting colder...
Even a Charon has limits on cold tolerance... The temperature will be down by twenty degrees this evening. We might lose a few kids to the cold. *sigh*...
Hello.
Greetings, my dear patron! Did you enjoy the play? You must be hungry after sitting through the show for three hours! Would you like some snacks and drinks?
Or perhaps you were captivated by the thrilling performance — how about a poster with the thespians' signatures?

options.content: How's business today? Will it cover your heating expenses for the night?
These are hardly enough for me. I'm a big eater.

talks.content: Your concern is appreciated. I can either afford enough food or fuel. Guess for some people, having it all isn't an option.
Then think of them as appetisers! There isn't much, but the flavor is definitely top-notch!
Okay, let's see what you've got.
A special edition poster signed by Vitti, Tales of Icelake souvenir albums, glacial meltwater, theatre-themed popcorn... and refreshing beer!
Don't you worry! This barely contains any alcohol and won't get you drunk!
That's hard to say... Do you happen to know Mr Buck the playwright?
Of course I do! Mr Buck frequents the theatre and is one of my most cherished patrons! Despite being a noble, he actually respects Charon kids like me. Mr Buck is one fine gentleman!
I know people make fun of Mr Buck, but unlike most people, he genuinely deserves respect.
That may be true, but I doubt it gives you the right to sneak into his house through the window and pour beer into his milk.
H—How did you know?
(Just as I thought.)
Mr Buck has a habit of writing his works at night. Your actions have delayed his progress for a month, so he hired me to find the mysterious "Inspiration Stealer".

options.content: You don't hate him and you stole nothing from him. Let me guess why you sneaked into his home in the middle of the night.

talks.content: Your business income isn't enough to cover your needs through the winter. Mr Buck might not be wealthy, but he is a noble and his house is warm enough. So, you sneaked into Mr Buck's home for the heating.
As for why you chose Mr Buck — even the smallest amount of alcohol makes him doze off. You could then sleep in his house without the fear of freezing to death. Am I right?
Ugh... You are indeed a great detective. You've got every detail right.
You might as well arrest me. I'm truly sorry for what I did. Though if I hadn't done it, I wouldn't be here for you to arrest...
I don't get to decide what to do with you. I'm taking you to my client.
I no longer have to worry about the cold winter. Thank you so much, Phoxhunter.
Greetings. I haven't seen you around before. Have you just arrived at Icelake? Is there anything you seek from this old lady?

options.content: Emma has a message for you. Something came up and she can't meet you today, but she wanted you to have this.

talks.content: (The doll, though crudely made, captures Belinda's essence. The old Charon lady's eyes light up with joy as she gently caresses the doll.)
I can feel the plaza's essence in this doll... Ah, my memory eludes me! It's Memorial Week, filled with all sorts of events...
Thank you very much, {性别:young man|young lady}.
(She observes you silently for a long moment.)
You seem to be carrying a heavy burden. I smell the ocean's breeze and tides on you, and the lingering warmth in your palm... it is fading...
Every moment you spend in this city is entwined in confusion and sorrow. You try to hide your pain, keeping your sorrows buried deep away from others...
Pardon me for this intrusion, but have you recently lost someone dear?

options.content: You are a Charon with special abilities?
I don't believe in superstitions and I don't understand a word you say.

talks.content: Indeed. It is rare for Charons to reach my age.
Your soul is in pain.
You don't have to put on an act. I see the pain you hide.
Though I'm unsure how to ease your suffering, an old saying might provide some comfort...
"They don their boots to traverse as Fate retracts her spindle. Doubt and uncertainty dost confound, but what is lost may come around."
It's the epilogue from The Spindle of the Goddess of Fate... The hero, having lost everything, reunites with all they had lost in the realm of duality... Are you suggesting we'll meet again?
Consider it a token of gratitude for bringing the doll. You are clever, as I've seen... You'll unravel the meaning on your own.
And one more thing — every soul who finds their way here gets a little gift from me. Just bring me a piece of wire that's been touched by your presence. No rush. I'll be here.
Touched by my presence...? Hmm. Not exactly sure what that means... But anything I've worn or handled should count, right?
There should be plenty of scrap wire lying around in Glevum Pit. I'll try my luck there.
(Belinda takes the wires from you and crafts it into a girl's silhouette. You can see that the handicraft resembles Berenica.)
My skills are modest. I see only shadows and cannot be sure if this resembles the one you yearn for. I hope it brings you comfort.
It is my sincere wish that you are reunited.
(You leave Belinda's tent, now understanding why Emma treasures this place. Belinda's powers may be limited, but she uses them to mend souls and soothe wounds.)
Something is about to happen! We stand upon the frozen lake, yet we perceive only coldness, deep isolation, and the frigid rigidity of our surroundings.
But we all know a dark tide is rising, gaining strength. One day it will consume everything we cherish. But before that day comes, I shall journey to the source that has been prophesied.
How are you today? May fortune and happiness accompany you.
Something is about to happen! We stand upon the frozen lake, yet we perceive only coldness, deep isolation, and the frigid rigidity of our surroundings.
But we all know a dark tide is rising, gaining strength. One day it will consume everything we cherish. But before that day comes, I shall journey to the source that has been prophesied.
I no longer have to worry about the cold winter. Thank you so much, Phoxhunter.
Tsk. A new face.
(The man before you squints, his lips cracked and dry, as he gruffly spits out his words.)
Tell me. Who sent you here?

options.content: The silver coins in my pocket sent me here.

talks.content: (Answering a question with another question always works.)
(It is obvious that he's waiting for someone.)
(I don't know what he meant, but that's an answer that no one will refuse.)
(The man broods silently for a while, assessing you. His posture decrepit as he raises his head with an audible creak.)
You smooth talker.
(He snorted, but he seemed to be satisfied with your answer.)
I don't care who the fixer is. You're here for the stuff in my pocket, ain't that right?
(He opens his collar to reveal a dull iron piece.)
(After showing it, he quickly conceals it again, looking around warily.)
Calibre 4. Double barrelled. Single shot. No Charon or Filthoid can survive a blast from this baby.
(His lip curls, as if he's just discussing the uses of a pesticide.)
You can have it for free, but I'll need you to do something for me.
Cut the crap. You're here for this piece of metal, ain't that right?
Do the job, and it's yours. I can even give you extra money.

options.content: (Well, can't let it fall into the wrong hands...)
(It looks like a handy piece. I gotta get it...)

talks.content: Fine, I'm in. What's the deal?
Good. I'll give you a location. Kill everything there except for a woman.
So... A bad romance, huh?
None of your beeswax. Just get it done.
(The man tightens his collar and licks his dried lips, unwilling to utter another word.)
What do you want?
Something is about to happen! We stand upon the frozen lake, yet we perceive only coldness, deep isolation, and the frigid rigidity of our surroundings.
But we all know a dark tide is rising, gaining strength. One day it will consume everything we cherish. But before that day comes, I shall journey to the source that has been prophesied.
Not all who dwell in the light live with a clear conscience.
(The girl stands at the corner with her head down. She looks very upset.)
It's you...
Were those your... classmates?
Yeah... I'm sorry... Really sorry... I messed up again.
Were they picking on you?
No... It's all my fault...
I can't do anything right. Both my mom and my teachers say I'm stupid.
My classmates are smart. They said that the reason I'm stupid is because I'm a Charon, and my parents hid my horns with magic.
It's all my fault... I shouldn't have showed up among Solas...
(You know that is a blatant lie. It also brings up unpleasant memories of what happened to you and Berenica on Purgatorio Island.)
(Those malicious acts may have been invited because of your weakness and differences, or, perhaps they just happened — the perpetrators only wanted to vent their hatred and you were just unlucky.)
(But this girl is more helpless than you. She didn't even have a friend like Berenica to share the pain.)

options.content: Why bother playing with them? You should give them a thrashing.
They lied. Don't believe a word they say.

talks.content: It isn't my fault...?
Huh...?
Huh...?
The fault lies with those who are mean to others.
Since they call you a demon, you might as well act like one.
They came up with a lie and made fun of you. But...
There's nothing to be afraid of. Fight back.
Let's go back and confront them.
Since they call you a demon, you might as well act like one.
See? That's all they can do.
...Yeah!
Thanks for helping me... You looked really cool throwing those punches!

options.content: And you seem to be really good at spouting insults. Practice when you have the chance. You'll get better.
You flatter me. The most important lesson is that you learned to stand up for yourself.

talks.content: R—Really? I... I just said the things that I'd wanted to say but couldn't.
Thank you so much. I've never felt so relieved and happy in my life!
You're welcome. Your classmates should leave you alone for a while. I'll walk you home. Here, this is my address — come find me if they give you trouble again.
I don't want to go home...!
I'm a Charon and I want to stay with my people...
Don't you see that? They acted all tough and mighty towards you, but once someone stronger shows up, they just run away.
They're not as strong as they pretend to be. Likewise, their words are not as truthful as they seem. Faye, don't listen to them. You're a hundred percent Sola.
Remember, never doubt yourself just because someone says bad things about you... My family taught me this, and I hope you'll keep it in mind too.
(The girl blinks her eyes in confusion. She probably doesn't understand everything you just said, but her expression softens.)
Okay... If that's what you say, I'll try my best! But before I leave, I still have a teensy-weensy request...
May I touch your horn?
Thank you!
Alright then. I won't touch it. But can I at least get a better look...?
(The girl carefully extends her frail hand and touches the horn on your head.)
(She carefully approaches you and studies the horn on your head.)
So this is what a real Charon horn looks like...
It's red and really delicate... it even reflects the sunlight. It looks way cuter than my pigtails.
You're the first to tell me that. But my pigtails are all messed up now... I have to braid them again.
(The girl takes out a comb from her bag. She then carefully combs and re-braids her pigtails. Once she's done, she lifts them up.)
Now, do they look like demon horns?

options.content: Actually, they look more like goat horns...

talks.content: Heheh.
Haha. That's good, too.
I have plenty of hairbands in my pocket. Can I braid a pigtail for you?
Come on, just squat down a little...
Please! I wanna see how it looks!
(You feel the girl slightly tugging your hair. She combs your hair very gently. You don't have to worry about losing any.)
(The girl stands on her toes and pushes you down to reach your hair. She seems a lot more positive and energetic than before.)
Done! Wow, you look so pretty with pigtails!
Too bad I don't have a mirror...
Ah...! I know! I can draw a picture of you.
(The girl opens her backpack and takes out a notebook. She then tries to draw a nice picture of you.)
Oh, I forgot to ask — what's your name?
Okay, {nickname}! I'll always remember you. Here, keep this picture I drew of you. See you around!
...That is some modern abstract art.
(The girl is about to leave but she suddenly turns around and gives you a serious gaze.)
Oh yeah... While I was combing your hair, I suddenly remembered something.
They kept telling me that Charons are demon's children who are stupid, evil, and are always doing bad things...
I don't think those words are true.
They were just lies made up as an excuse to bully your kind, right?
You must have... suffered way more pain than I ever have.
If there's anything I can do to help in the future, please do let me know... It's not because we're the same kind, but because we're friends.
That white-haired demon is so strong!
Umm... This doesn't look good! We better scoot!
Wait.
For your information, Faye has signed a demon contract with me. If you ever mess with her again, I will show up immediately to deal with you.
You... you...! Hmph!
My classmates still don't like me, but I'm not afraid of them anymore! All thanks to you!
Great, {nickname} isn't around today...
Looking for me?
...Whoa! Speak of the devil!

options.content: Kevin, there's someone illegally selling Phoxene in the slums.

talks.content: (The phone by the gate suddenly rings. Kevin leaps up like a startled hare and quickly picks up the phone.)
Kevin speaking. What? Suspicious guy in the city? Got it. I'm on my way.
...Probably the one you just mentioned. Could you lead the way?
Travel permit check — oi, I'm talking to you! Got your travel permit on you?

options.content: (Tearfully explain that you're a law-abiding citizen who's once again forgotten your travel permit.)
(Hand over the travel permit Camilla forged.)
Mr Kevin, you wouldn't want your superiors finding out about that incident by Lamenting Lake, would you...?

talks.content: Oh, spare me — I've heard that so many times my ears are calloused. Off you go, and don't make a spectacle of yourself.
Travel permit verified. You may pass.
Alright, alright! Fine — you can go, just go!
For once... no trouble...

options.content: (Famous last words — something's bound to happen now.)

talks.content: (A shrill ring erupts by the gate. Kevin jumps like a startled rabbit and scrambles to answer.)
Alright, alright... Yes — understood!
(After a brief exchange, Kevin lowers the phone and gestures for you to pass.)
If that's all, off you go. So much for a quiet shift...
Why does trouble always find you...?
Oi! Permit — oh, it's you. Go on, off you go.
Good luck with your investigations, Detective!
Once you've investigated the stories behind them, come back and tell me what you think about Icelake!
Please help me gather the ingredients. I'll use this time to refine the recipe.
While you're out fishing, I'll brainstorm some enhancements to the recipe.
Is everything going smooth, Detective?
It was so hard to leave when I was young, and now I can't go back...
Take care.
Howdy, Super Bros!
"The Noctoyagers"... Hmm, sounds pretty good! If other teams were like you, there would be plenty of space on the board.
Keep it up. Try to best those long, tongue-twisting names and get to the top.
You here, ask about trains? Careful, mean gatekeeper girl here!

options.content: Seems par for the course in this city. You'll get used to it after a while.
You can't even throw a comeback?

talks.content: Enough for me! Want to leave, very, very much!
Still learning! Language here, different from home!
(This ticket seller looks tough. But considering you'll eventually need to leave Icelake, crossing paths with her seems inevitable... Should you take action now?)
(Perhaps this "intel" you got from Margie could help break the ice...)

options.content: Excuse me, I think I can smooth things over here.

talks.content: Thank you! You are good! I watch you handle this!
Child, even though the path ahead is uncertain, always proceed with determination.
May Mother Embla bless you.
Aaaahhhh, this is way too high! I can't tell if it's higher than the Hall of Adjudication in Huaxu... No, my fear of heights is back...
Don't look out there yet. Just stare at your feet and calm down.
Whew...Whew... Now I feel much better.
Seriously, what was the Empire architects thinking back then, making walls of such towering height?
Hmm?
Why is that? If I recall correctly, according to the official chronicles, Icelake started out as a Charon settlement.

The First Emperor, Dis Galea — known as Dis Ⅰ — came to this land after the Great Migration. At first, he hoped to seek peace with the Charon tribes dwelt here. But his brother was beguiled with a promise of a feast, and slain by the locals.
That's why Dis Ⅰ believed that Charons were demons, and led his knights to subdue them, declaring the so-called "Silverpeace."
But if so, against whom were these towering walls raised? Filthoids? Or perhaps Charons of that times were still resisting?
Got inspired again, did you?
Not exactly inspiration, but something just feels... strange. Mr Qiu always told us: let no moment of strangeness pass, for therein the truth may lie concealed.
Anyway, thanks a lot, truly! Now I feel ready to write a field report full of passion!
Without you, I'd probably still think Icelake held no archaeological values and write those superficial reports, like a fool overlooking all that matters.
How blind I was! Wait, could you be the true hidden archaeology master in Icelake?

options.content: I was hoping to keep a low profile...
I'm just an ordinary Phoxhunter passing by.
Spare me your flattery. My reward — now.

talks.content: Woww... You really do have the aura of a master — no doubt about it!
I get it. You're trying to keep your identity secret from others.
Let me think... What reward would be worthy of a master like you?
I got it! Please wait for me at the city gate.
哎呦……！里边这儿的老鼠也太多了！
Good day, you look great with this flower... That kid would have said so, if she were still here.
My daughter. Psyche. That was her name.
She mentioned a "new friend" in her letters. You look just as she described... but forgive me, if I'm mistaken.
That you're clever. And brave. She said you ventured into Glevum Pit your very first day in Icelake... Of everyone her age, she said you were the strongest. But more importantly...
(You turn away, almost running. It's a shared, silent wound you're not ready to face.)
"{性别:He|She}'s different from most people in Icelake. {性别:He|She} still holds on to something we all lost long ago — a yearning for justice and freedom."
"Being with {性别:him|her} shows me there's a different way to live."
That's what she wrote. Word for word.
(She recites it by heart — clearly, she's read that letter more times than she can count.)
I'm so sorry. I couldn't...
Don't apologise, child. I could see it. She was happy, with you by her side. That's all we could've asked for. It's us who should be thanking you.
Please, take these flowers. Our blessings go with you.
Travel safe. Our blessings go with you.
Thank you, kind soul. You've saved my life. I must be going — my patients in Vivar are waiting.
You're a doctor? Would you happen to be Dr Elinor?
That's me. Are you looking for me?
I heard you rescued a girl in the northern mountains recently.
Ah, yes. You've seen her in Icelake, then? Is she doing all right?
Physically, she seems fine. But... she's lost her memory. I was wondering — did she have anything on her when you found her? Something that might help figure out who she is?
She did, actually. I'd been meaning to follow up after this house call. If you're willing to help, that would be wonderful.
Here — this was with her.
I need to get going. Thank you again for saving my life.
(If the words in this diary are true... then the truth is clear at last.)
(Not only has the lost girl's real identity come to light — so too has the fate of Elsa's daughter, Annie.)

(...Annie has tragically passed away, while the other girl, Alice, who ended up with Annie's clothes, has survived. Although Alice made it through the ordeal in the snowy mountains, the severe fevers she suffered afterwards took away her memories.)
Once I've recovered, I will start my next adventure.
Once my mother gets better, I'll take her to see the beauty in the great outdoors!
This time, I'll go with pink ones!
(The woman smiles as she picks up the carefully chosen pink blooms. Looking up, she notices you.)
Hello there. Are you here to buy flowers too?
Take a look? Pink flowers like these are quite rare, you know.

options.content: Thank you, I think they're lovely too.
Oh no, I can't stand pink!

talks.content: Hehe, of course!
You can have them if you like.
Oh dear, I'm so sorry to hear that.
(She reaches out, deftly takes a few more stems from the shelf, pays for them along with her own, and hands them to you.)
I'm sure he wouldn't have minded either.
Well, it's true. Not everyone likes pink, I suppose...
Here you are.
Are these flowers for someone?
Now that you mention it, perhaps he didn't either... But never mind! Let's just pretend he did.
No need to thank me. Just think of it as you sharing in his good fortune.
Yes. I have a faerie friend, much like you with horns, and these are for him.
Oh, that's what he called himself.
Well, "faerie" was his word for it.
Speaking of which,has the wind picked up outside?

options.content: I can make wind, even if there isn't any.

talks.content: I see... No matter, I'll check for myself later.
That's wonderful.
Really? You're that powerful? That's very kind of you.
I need to wait for the wind to pick up before I can give him the flowers.

options.content: Why do you need the wind?
Is your friend a wind faerie, by any chance?
Is this some special kind of ritual?

talks.content: Because when the wind blows, the flowers can float up into the sky.
An interesting thought! Perhaps he is.
Well... it's a ritual for sending thoughts to someone.
That friend of mine... he went up to the sky several years ago.
Today is the annual day of remembrance.
In Charon belief, the Misty Sea is where souls go. If you wish to remember him, sending the flowers onto the water would make more sense.
Well... I know. But he was different.
(The woman falls silent, gazing out the window, her eyes filled with a gentle nostalgia.)
I first met him outside the city. We were the same age, and our personalities just clicked, so we became fast friends.
He told me he was a "faerie" from the sky... Hehe, truthfully, I knew all along he was Charon. But every time I saw him trying so hard to keep up the story, I couldn't bear to spoil it for him.
Besides, he really was just like a faerie from the stories — he knew so many things I didn't, and always had endless fascinating tales to tell.

options.content: So he was playing the part of a faerie his whole life?

talks.content: Yes! He's the best friend ever.
Sounds a bit childish when you put it like that, doesn't it?
It always bothered me a little... wondering how we would finally talk about it, once we grew up and passed the age where believing in fairy tales came naturally.
Whether I brought it up or he did, just imagining it felt so awkward...
But in the end, we never reached that point. He left before we came of age.
Do you think... he might have chosen to leave at that precise time because he knew? What a gentle soul he was...
(The woman strokes the soft petals, gently lowering her gaze. You can't quite decipher the emotion on her face.)

options.content: Coming of age... Did he start showing signs of Deterioration?

talks.content: It's okay. It's been years.
Then... thank you.

So, that's why you cast the flowers into the sky?
Indeed. Since that was the story he wanted to tell me, I choose to believe that his final resting place isn't the Misty Sea, but the vast blue sky.
As long as I scatter the petals to the wind, he'll feel my thoughts.

options.content: I hope he receives your flowers.
I'm sure he will receive them.

talks.content: ...Thank you.
Looking back now, I think he probably knew all along that I had seen through his little charade.
A story woven from lies, ending with a lie... doesn't that seem rather fitting, in a way?
Right, I'd best be off outside the city walls to keep my promise to him before it gets dark.
Goodbye, little faerie. May your own story have a true and happy ending.
Hello again, little faerie. Lovely weather we're having, isn't it?
I am Icelake's foremost Geniemon scholar! If you have any questions about them, feel free to— Oh, it's you. Uh, is—is there anything I can help you with?

options.content: What do you know about Paniemon?
How's life as a Geniemon scholar?

talks.content: You mean that incredibly intelligent Geniemon?

Speaking of which, I really appreciate that you and Truffle went easy on me back then.
But you might be able to track it down by following the traces it leaves behind.
Blimey, everyone's working so hard!
Unlike me... I just snooze in the sun.

options.content: Everyone lives life their own way.
Napping in the sun — now that's living!
It's a long-term investment in your health, isn't it?

talks.content: Haha, you really get it.

A Luno's gotta help people. I get antsy if I'm not helping someone. It feels off.

options.content: (Ask Lunolaze about the secret to getting rich.)

You could try falling off a cliff yourself.

options.content: You're kidding! How come I never get that lucky when I fall off cliffs?

The end draws near... it draws near...

The flowers at the shop are dull, fading to bleached-white heather...
The cats in the square are no longer soft and fluffy. They're hard and smooth... like plaster statues...
The bakery can't make fluffy bread anymore. No matter what they do, it just turns into black sludge...
My favourite ice lollies aren't even cold anymore. They turn all sticky and glue up your throat...
Everyone's getting taller... whiter... just like a Luno...
In the end...
The flower shop lady, the baker, the lolly seller... Everyone will turn into a Luno!

options.content: Lunos are great. I want to be one too.

talks.content: Your hair... your clothes... your height... Are you turning into a Luno already?!
The end's here... It really is. It's all over now.

The end... it's begun...
Kind soul... I beg you... Anything you can spare... I've nothing left...

options.content: (Poor old soul. Give him some money.)

You're fit enough to work — you should be doing so.

talks.content: Ah... thank you, young one.
You... Ah, well.
Work... ha. I used to have a decent job, once...
Never know if an old man like me will wake up tomorrow... but at least I'm getting a proper meal today.
Your eyes, {性别:lad|lass}... did they do a number on you too?
But what good did it do? Sometimes they snatch your job as easily as they snatch the coins from this bowl.
Never mind. Go on, take them. You probably need them more than I do.
Begging in a fancy house, begging in the street... what's the difference?
Live well, yeah? This world's cruel... crueler still to the good ones.
(The girl stares out of the window, lost in thought. Her gaze is fixed on something far away, as if searching the vast, empty sky.)
(You sense a stillness about her, something out of place for her age — an air of stagnation, of slow decay.)
(A part of you worries she might do something rash, another part is just curious what she's looking for. Either way, you decide to break the silence.)

Hello?
If you want something, just get on with it.
Oh, no, it's nothing. It's just... you seem to be staring into the distance. Looking for something?
Am I...? Maybe I wasn't looking at anything at all.
Just... drifting. Aimlessly.

options.content: I sometimes find myself spacing out like that. It's quite calming.
Fancy a change of subject? Like... what's for supper?

talks.content: "Sometimes"... It seems we're not so alike, you and I...
Anything... I know that's not a real answer, but I honestly don't feel like eating.
(The girl lowers her head, saying no more.)
(Everyone has struggles no one else can see. In the end, we all have to face them alone.)
(Maybe she hasn't found the courage yet. Best to let her be for now, you think to yourself.)
Table... done. Floor... done. What's left... the handrail. Yes, the handrail.
(The boy is muttering to himself, looking stressed. His hands gesture about frantically.)
...Can you step aside?
Sorry?
The handrail. I still need to wipe it. You're in the way.
(You follow his agitated gaze to the staircase handrail. It might not be new, but as far as you can tell, it's already gleaming and utterly spotless.)

options.content: It looks perfectly clean to me.

talks.content: It isn't! I haven't wiped it today, so it's definitely not clean...
(Taking the hint, you shrug and step aside, letting him get back to his endless, frantic cleaning.)
And the picture frames upstairs, the bookcase, the lamp... and... and other things...
Please, just leave me to it... Don't you have anything else to do?
Stay away from me... I don't know anything!!
I only want to have a look at the pocket watch. Perhaps I can fix it.
It's precious to you, isn't it?
You... you can really fix it?

options.content: Will you let me have a try?
There must be watchmakers in town. We could ask for their help.

talks.content: I don't know...
Could you...
Hunt... what am I supposed to do?
No... I can't trust outsiders.
So, what happened to Hunt?
Just forget I said anything.
He...
Please, just leave. Don't come back.
No, I can't say. Please, just leave. Don't come back.
(The girl's sudden change of heart leaves you stumped. You search her eyes, hoping for some clue.)
(They are eyes full of sorrow and confusion, yet you see a flicker of conviction within them. You don't know where it comes from, or what it means, but you understand this is why she won't talk.)

♪ White snow is her birth-flow, and twilight her warm cord aglow.
She bears grand and pain to iron cradle — beneath the mountain, in the cold...
We meet again, dear {性别:sir|miss}. You're a garnet on white sand. You must like it here. I do too.
Have you ever been inside the Galea Theatre?

options.content: I fought the Legion there once.

talks.content: Oh! How enviable... You must be well-off.
Ah... then I'm not the only one kept outside the gates.
You fought the Legion? Remarkable... You must have stories tucked away like old sheet music.
I've visited opera houses across Luca, but here in Hyperborea... they always turn me away.
I knew Charons had it rough in this city, but I never imagined the supervision levies for public spaces would be so steep...

Still — I was lucky to arrive just in time for the Silvercandle Carnival. It's the city's one day when even paupers like me can step through the theatre doors for free. Tragic, though... to hear there'd been a shootout inside. Absolutely dreadful.
Even so, I gathered plenty of sheet music! The bookshop prices were fair, and a few kind souls let me trade verses for pages. And one mysterious person... even taught me a famous aria.
A few nights ago, I was leaning against a wall under the moonlight, humming a melody I'd picked up from a second-hand score. It was simple enough — soft, easy to carry on the wind.
When I finished, I heard knocking — on the other side of the wall. Rhythmic. Intentional. Bards are always sensitive to rhythm... I knew it wasn't random.
It was code — old knock code, passed down long ago. Just two kinds of taps, but enough to send meaning through stone.
They told me I'd sung it wrong. It was a well-known operatic piece here — but I hadn't read the libretto, so I'd missed its feeling and heart.
They couldn't speak or sing. I don't know why. But they used that rhythm to teach me how to sing it true.
And when I had finally mastered the song, I ran to the other side of the wall to thank them... Only to find they were already gone.

options.content: I think I know that person.
This city's full of kooky characters.

talks.content: Oh, how lucky!
That it is... and full of kooky tales, too.
If it's not too much trouble... would you thank them for me? And send them my best wishes, too. I don't know why they couldn't sing — but I'm sure they loved music, deeply.
The opera here is quite unlike Luca's.
...Sure, I will.
Luca's opera is fire. Aethyrie's — wind.
But Hyperborea... its opera is the earth itself. Heavy, vast, and full of pain...
My friend and I will be leaving soon. But before that... I want to write one last song for this place.
What made us who we are?
This one's the most fascinating — it says everything in the Misty Sea is caught in an endless cycle of life and death. What do you think, Idy—
Ah! It's you! I remember — we spoke right here, didn't we?
Have you seen my friend? Red hair, always drifting in and out like the wind... She was just here a moment ago.

options.content: I haven't seen anyone like that around.

talks.content: Thanks anyway. I'll wait a bit — she has a habit of vanishing... then turning up out of nowhere.
We've been gathering Charon myths these past few days. It's surprising how openly people speak of them here.
Charons are shunned here in Hyperborea, but back in my homeland, Elysium, they're venerated as divine messengers enthroned in sacred halls. But to speak those old myths aloud... is dangerous there.
Do you know much about the myths of the Charon?
"Charon" means "those who came from the Misty Sea"...

The Misty Sea is the origin of all things. From it rose the Sacred Tree. Its canopy stretched across the heavens — and each of its branches became a Heaventree. Its roots, meanwhile, cradled the world.
The tree bloomed with white flowers, and from them stepped forth Mother Embla. She created all things — and from her came Father Ask. Together, they gave birth to the first of the Charons.
Yet Ask, bearer of <W>the power of death</>, became a vessel of calamity. In the end, it was he who brought ruin to the world — the cataclysm we call Ragnarok.
In that final hour, Mother Embla — keeper of <H>the power of life</> — gathered her children and sheltered them. Her soul scattered into the sea... and at last, returned to the Misty Sea.
Ask's body became the land and his arms, upraised, became the mountains, still reaching for the gods... who no longer come.

options.content: That's... kind of a sad story.

talks.content: Mm... but there's another thread in the myths that caught my ear.
It says Ask and Embla were reborn after the world's end — in new forms, walking again in a new world.
And that their reborn selves would one day bring about another ending — and another beginning.
Thus the world turns, ever in circles. Life and death, again and again.

options.content: Seems that the ancients didn't like tragic endings either.

talks.content: But... what I keep wondering is — why was the storyteller so sure that the gods were reborn? Or rather... what makes Embla and Ask who they are?
Is it their bodies? Their souls? ...Or something else entirely?

Imagine this — just for a moment — that a great mage turned the land beneath our feet back into Ask's original form... Then who would truly be Father Ask? The one made of ancient earth? Or the one who bears his soul reborn?

options.content: The one with Ask's original body.
The one with Ask's original soul.
I don't think either one is really the original Ask.
Are all bards this pointlessly philosophical?

talks.content: Ah... so that's how you see it. Thank you. You've given me something new to ponder.
Most songs begin with a question that sounds pointless, don't they?
Thank you for your time, dear {性别:sir|miss}. You're a spark on a cold wick. I've come to love these myths. I think... I've found a song inside them, at last.
Thank you, dear {性别:sir|miss}, for giving me the line I needed. You're a rose blooming on the tundra.

♪ Furnace-fire burns the dawn, tipping out the fortress of iron 'n' snow.
Gears sing in hymns, devour the stars, hailing the great age of ice in north—
Hmm? Were you talking to me...?
Thank you, kind traveller! But the song's not quite finished yet... Perhaps we could find its ending together?
Oh — apologies if I disturbed you! Though I did check with the guard over there, and he said there's no law against bards singing in the square.
Now, how should the final line go...?
I think it should be about the wind. Every place has its own wind...

The wind in Elysium smells of frankincense, melting into evening prayers. In Luca, it's turpentine from painter's lofts, and caramel wafting from cafés. In Aethyrie, the scent is ink laced with wild mint...
So — what does the wind smell like, here in Hyperborea?

options.content: It smells like iron and fire.

talks.content: Hmm... you may be right. This city was born of steel — a forest forged, not grown.
So true! They say three-quarters of this city is made of snow. Locals told me it's always snowing in Icelake — only thaws three months a year.
"Tears?" Hmm... That's a line I haven't used yet...
The wind may sting with cold, but it hums with gears and hisses with flame. And when you touch it... it burns.
And snow always has its partner: the wind. They dance together — nature's perfect duet!
Like the barrel of a soldier's rifle — even when their face is cold as stone.
Thank you, dear {性别:sir|miss} — you've given me the line I needed. You're a rose blooming on the tundra. I think I can finally finish this song.

That day, the wind drifting through this square... it felt like it was weeping too.

Should I go pick some Sky Lilies to put in the vase?
Master! You must be the fated encounter I've been waiting for!

options.content: What "fated encounter"? Am I supposed to get something out of this?
Is this... some kind of role-playing?
Right — one look at you and I can tell you're a once-in-a-century martial prodigy.

talks.content: Huh? Of course not... The gains from a fated encounter aren't something you can share.
Huh? What's that supposed to mean?
Really?! I knew I was destined for greatness!
Ah— wait. I get it. You're testing my character!
Uh... it's a kind of game. People pretend to be characters in a story and act things out. You never did that as a kid?
Wait— no, no, I'm getting carried away. I'm shouting like a madman... how rude of me. Master, please allow me to bow to you!
My mistake. I almost let a little greed cloud my mind. True martial skill should serve the world — how could I keep it to myself?
Pretend? No way. If we're doing something, we do it for real. Pretending is dull.
Hold on — I never agreed to be your master!
So what exactly is this "fated encounter" you keep mentioning?
Let me explain. A few days ago, I spotted two seasoned martial artists being chased by some vicious beast. I wanted to help, but I was too weak — I couldn't even catch up to them.
After they ran past, I found this torn manual on the ground. I figured it had to contain some secret technique powerful enough to shake the martial world. Their trouble must've been because of it!
I tried telling my shifu, but he completely lost it — said I was wasting my time on violent nonsense instead of studying. Then he sent me out to these barren hills to "reflect on my actions".
Studying...? So your shifu teaches literature, not martial arts?
I admit it — my heart's always been set on the martial path. But every time I bring up martial arts, people get all tense and start quoting things like "To wound or kill — this must not be done."
My family only hired a scholar to teach me. I've never even seen a real martial arts master.
My shifu doesn't know any martial arts himself, but he's always treated me kindly. Thinking back now, he must've thought the manual looked suspicious — that's probably why he was so upset.
(You take a look at the "manual". No matter how you look at it, it's just a martial-arts comic book — with BANNED stamped loudly across the cover.)
(With a bit of deduction, the whole situation becomes clear: someone out in the wild got attacked by a Sable Bi'an, dropped their comic, and this young man happened to pick it up.)
Still, meeting you turned my bad luck around. With your guidance, once I master great skills, I'll fight for justice, save the martial world, and stop Huaxu from falling apart!
So... you picked up a random book, your teacher panicked, and now you're stuck out here doing "self-reflection"?
Exactly. You truly are perceptive, master.
I even tried everything the book said about fated encounters — throwing myself off cliffs to find hidden caves, triggering traps to stumble into ancient tombs... none of it worked.
This was the last method I hadn't tried yet, so I came to the spot mentioned in the book to wait for one... and then you appeared.

Dressed in pristine white, drifting in like an immortal — you must be a true master! Your eyes must be hiding some extraordinary power — that's why you keep one concealed, isn't it? Please, allow me to bow to you!
(He's completely swept up in his own fantasy — cliffs, caves, tombs... this is a whole new level of absurd.)
(You've met people who are obsessed with stories before, but someone who mixes fiction with reality this thoroughly... that's a first.)
(Faced with someone this ridiculous yet oddly sincere, the best approach might be to just...)

options.content: Masters who walk outside worldly norms don't fuss over rules anyway — and he is quite a character. What's the harm in teaching him a move or two?
Time to drag him back to reality.

talks.content: In that case... why don't you start by cutting that waterfall in half?
I think your shifu had a point.
Huh? M—Master, isn't cutting a waterfall a bit too much for a starter like me...?
Huh? Master, what do you mean...?
Ahem. Training in the great arts is never easy. If you back down at the first step, what will you do when things actually get difficult?
If you truly want to master great skills, you need real training. Sitting around waiting for miracles won't get you anywhere.
Y—You're right, but...
Besides, Huaxu forbids violence. Even if you learned a whole arsenal of techniques, where would you use them? Push things too far and a Bi'an will show up to punish you.
Look at you — all hesitation and no resolve. How are you supposed to learn anything formidable like this? By whining?
Channel that energy into studying instead. Return the comic, clear things up with your shifu, and focus on your lessons. That's as much guidance as I can offer.
I was ready to make an exception and give you a little guidance because you seemed sincere — but your willpower is disappointingly mediocre.
That's exactly what my shifu said... so everything in the book really is made up?
...You're right, master. I shouldn't shy away just because it's difficult. I'll head into the mountains and start training right now!
But... but even if that's true... did you have to say it that harshly...?
(You watch the young man run off and give a small, satisfied nod. If he ever becomes someone remarkable, he'll probably remember the "master" who set him straight in these mountains.)
(In short... well done, you.)
Keep looking... there must be something I've overlooked.
Are you searching for something?
Hm? I didn't realise anyone else was nearby.
Friend, Sable Bi'an appear in this area rather frequently. It's not a place ordinary travellers should approach without caution.
Thanks for the warning. I've been here before — I can take care of myself.
And you? Why take the risk of walking around here?
Exploring, investigating, searching for archaeological clues... call it what you will. In essence, I'm examining whether anything of historical value remains here.
Something valuable? So you're treasure-hunting for money?
Haha. Many people do make a living that way, but please don't mistake me for one of them. I'm not seeking wealth. What I'm after is insight.
Fragments of old writings, components from ancient mechanisms... things others dismiss as worthless often contain hints. They help me piece together what might have taken place here.
So, friend — do you know anything about the history of this place?

options.content: (What happened here? You feel like someone mentioned it to you before.)

talks.content: I vaguely remember — this used to be a battlefield, right? Two groups fought here and a lot of people died. That's why it gets so creepy at night... and all those ghost-story rumours.
Precisely.

I didn't expect an outlander to know anything about this place. Either your memory is impressive, or you have a genuine interest in these old events. See? People are drawn to history without even noticing it.
So what actually happened here?
This is where the Battle of Shuli took place. Several centuries ago, the Jishu Sect rose in revolt here, and the Xuanheng Sect sent forces to suppress them. In the end, none of them survived.
It left a considerable mark on Huaxu's history, influencing many decisions in the ages that followed — or so the official records state.
But the curious thing is that those records are rather vague about how it all began — almost as though something has been deliberately glossed over.

options.content: So you think the official record isn't telling the whole truth?
Dig too deeply and you'll get silenced — that's how these stories usually go.

talks.content: Hah! I wouldn't frame it as doubt — I'd call it a hypothesis.
Haha. You jest. Under the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, no one in Huaxu has to worry about matters like that — the Bi'an and the Magistrates of Yingtian will see to my safety.
Even so, if the truth really were just what the official records claim, it wouldn't be nearly as intriguing.
History shows only what it chooses to. Over time, the truth becomes distorted — shaped to serve the interests of whoever is recording it.
So I prefer to take what little imagination I have and picture how events might actually have unfolded. Tell me, friend — what possibilities do you think there are?

options.content: I'd sooner trust the records — unless there's clear evidence they're wrong.
If we're making bold guesses... I'd say Xuanheng started it.
It was aliens disguised as humans who started it!

talks.content: A prudent and measured stance.
Heh... there are scholars with a conspiratorial bent who think along those lines.
Hah! Well, that's a possibility too.
But speculation is only the first step. To lift the veil, you need the second step — evidence.
To test my hypothesis, I joined the Ministry of Works. It allowed me to gain a deeper understanding of how the mechapuppets function and to learn more about what truly happened back then.
The masters there didn't take offence when I told them my intentions. Instead, they said the Jishu Sect is short on young people like me these days — and so they simply kept me.
You've done all this just to study the past?

I can't say what any of it will ultimately amount to, but once I began, I simply couldn't stop. Different clues link together in ways you wouldn't expect. Perhaps they'll lead to the truth, perhaps not — but my curiosity won't let me ignore them.
Well then, I should get back to searching for clues. It was a pleasure speaking with you.
I'll be staying in this area for a good while. If you come across anything, do let me know.
Ah, it's you. Have you discovered anything new?
That jar... the barley sugar inside... I'm... curious about the taste.
(The Wishen stares into the distance, unaware that you're standing nearby.)
(Perhaps the sound of your footsteps catches its attention. It drifts towards you and offers a greeting.)
Hello?
Hello... stranger.
Ah... you startled me... I was lost in thought... didn't notice.
Uh... hello. I didn't mean to disturb you...
You... can see me? That's rare... makes me happy.
I want to talk... To everyone. Please... help me. They can't see me... feels lonely.
You need help with something? Maybe I can.
You're kind. Thank you. At the market... the barley sugar... curious about the taste.

options.content: You recall that you still have a few pieces of barley sugar in your pack. You could share one with it.

talks.content: I've got a few with me — would you like to try one?
Wow... Thank you... truly...
(The Wishen accepts the sweet with a gentle, careful motion and lifts it towards what might once have been its mouth.)
(Its mirage-like form can hardly be called a body. You can't tell whether this gesture counts as eating — perhaps it's simply copying something it remembers from when it was alive.)
(As expected, the sweet slips straight through its form and falls into the dust below, taking with it the faint flicker of hope you saw a moment ago.)
Can't eat... can't taste... it feels sad...

options.content: Describe the taste of barley sugar for the Wishen.

talks.content: It feels soft at first, but becomes chewy when you bite into it. As the sweetness melts, there's a light, grain-like aroma that follows.
It's not as heavy or sugary as other sweets. It tastes gentle — like standing beside rice fields in early autumn, with the wind brushing through the stalks and carrying a faint scent of earth.
I don't understand... But it sounds... nice. So... it's good?
Yeah. It's a lovely taste.
My memories... blurry. When I was little, the other children ate sweets... and laughed. I wanted one too... but I had no money.
When I grew up, there was work... a family to care for... no time. I kept thinking, "next time... next time".
When I got old, my teeth were gone... I couldn't eat sweets anymore... I could only buy them for the children.
I wanted to try them... but everyone had duties. I couldn't be selfish... Sweets were for children... grown-ups had to work... keep going.
But even then... I never forgot. Still curious... what it tasted like.
Everyone ate them... and smiled. It must be a taste... that makes people happy...
You didn't have to shoulder everything alone. If you wanted a sweet, you could've just had one. No one would've blamed you.
I... could? I was... allowed?
Of course. It's just a tiny treat. If even that little bit of happiness isn't allowed... that'd be far too cruel.
(The Wishen falls silent. A lifetime of quiet longing seems to tremble faintly within its fading form.)
(Feelings long forgotten drift back to it for a moment, though you know they won't stay.)
(Its outline ripples gently, turning a little more transparent.)
(If another life awaits it... may it finally taste a piece of sweetness of its own.)
Hey there — I'm Ramon. You don't look local.
(A man — suspiciously friendly — calls out to you. After a quick look around, you realise he really is talking to you.)
(His unsolicited friendliness puts you slightly on edge. Still, this is Huaxu — with the Nine Chapters of Dafeng watching over everything, he's hardly likely to cause trouble.)

options.content: Respond to the suspiciously friendly man.

talks.content: Hello — I'm {Nickname}.
Straightforward enough. So, what are you then — a merchant, a traveller, or something else?
I'm a merchant from Hyperborea, here in Huaxu for business.
I'm from a small island called Purgatorio Island. I'm travelling through the countries of Atlasia at the moment.
I'm a Phoxhunter. I came to Huaxu on a special commission.

Hyperborea? Not the kindest place towards Charons, from what I've heard. A Charon engaged in international trade out of there — that's quite something. What goods do you handle? I can introduce you to a few contacts.
Purgatorio Island... can't say I've heard of it. Still, since you're in Huaxu, I can point you to some sights — and a few places to eat that people rave about.
Phoxhunter... right, that bounty-hunter sort of job from Hyperborea? Travelling abroad for work — that's dedication. If you run into trouble, just say the word. I might be able to help.
What's in it for you?
No need to be that wary. With the Nine Chapters of Dafeng watching over Huaxu, I couldn't harm you even if I wanted to.
And as for why I'm offering to help... well, look at me — I'm a foreigner too, just like you. I'm from Aethyrie. Heard of it?
I remember — the country covered in forests, right?
Never heard of it...
Good, that saves me explaining. Plenty of people haven't heard of my homeland, and giving the whole rundown every time gets tiring.
Aethyrie's south of Hyperborea and north of Elysium — a place of vast forests and plenty of scholars.

I came here hoping to study Huaxu's ways — its traditions, customs, all that — but the history, folklore, culture, the arts... everything turned out far richer than I'd expected. Before I realised it, I'd already been here over a decade.
Plenty of foreigners pass through Huaxu, but not many really get the place.
So I try to help them find their feet a bit quicker. You know how it is — when you're abroad, bumping into someone who's an outsider like you is strangely comforting, isn't it?
Uh... so you just talk to every foreigner who walks past? Is that your job? Some kind of guide?
My job? Well, I do act as a go-between for traders or officials now and then — keeps their conversations from going off the rails. They pay me for that.

Think about it: a Hyperborean blurting out something offensive to a Loongscion in a business meeting... or a Huaxu local making a poorly timed remark about seafood to someone from Luca — that could get ugly, right?
But don't worry — this isn't anything like that. I'm talking to you out of goodwill alone. Anything I offer is completely free.
Sorry... I do believe you. I just don't really understand why you'd go this far.
I understand. Everyone who first arrives feels the same — I did too.

But once you actually start speaking to people here, you notice something unique... a sort of openness. Because of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, people in Huaxu have this instinctive warmth and trust towards strangers.
And it isn't naive trust — it's a choice. They choose to extend goodwill, knowing full well they won't come to any harm.
I'm not saying my homeland is any worse, but honestly, I was really drawn to that atmosphere. It's how I think people across Atlasia ought to treat one another.
So I try to pass that mindset on to foreigners like me — let them bring a bit of it back home and spread it. Maybe the world ends up a little more peaceful.
Th—That's... quite a vision.
Hah! Well, I'll admit I've got my own reasons too. If the Empire and the Church weren't constantly at each other's throats, Aethyrie — my homeland — would have a much easier time of it, wouldn't it?
But honestly? I just enjoy being able to show goodwill without having to worry about any consequences.
Everyone likes to think they're a good person. And when you can actually prove it through what you do, it feels... rather nice.

Some people probably wouldn't say it out loud like that, but honestly, I just like feeling good about myself. And if someone else gets a bit of help out of it as well, that's a win in my book — wouldn't you say?
If you need anything while you're in Huaxu, just come and find me. I've built up quite a few connections over the years — and don't worry, I won't charge you a thing.
Then... thanks for that.
If you ever need help, just come to me.
Come now... don't cry. It's meant to be good news... good news...
I know, I know... it's just that my heart feels as empty as this house...
*sigh*...

options.content: What's happened? Is there anything I can do to help?
What sort of "good news" makes you cry like that? Are you putting it on?

talks.content: *sigh*... Tell me, do you know where Huaxu's Bi'an come from?

options.content: (Bi'an — guardians of Huaxu. They're born from...)

talks.content: Some Loongscions, once they come of age, enter a covenant with the Nine Chapters of Dafeng and become Bi'an.
Aye. So when someone becomes one, it's something their parents should be proud of.
Our firstborn became one. The neighbours all came round to congratulate us, and the missus and I were proud as anything.
But who'd have thought that when our second lad came of age, he'd become a Bi'an as well.
Two Bi'an from the same household... folk were full of envy, and we were smiling all through the celebration.
But once we came home and saw their rooms standing empty... there was only one thing I could feel — the place was just too quiet...
Sometimes, when I'm lying out in the yard, I can almost hear the boys again... telling me not to nod off by the door, saying their mother's calling me in for dinner.
But when I get up, there's no one there. All I see is my wife's hair growing greyer by the day... and her eyes dimming with the years.
In those days, our only comfort was our youngest — our third son.

He knew how much we missed his brothers, so he'd go out of his way to make things easier for us — help his mother tidy the house, take a walk with me, little things like that. He's the only reason this cold, quiet shack ever felt like a home again.
With him around, we could still carry on. Bit by bit, we made our peace with the fact that the older two were never coming back.
But then that cursed "good news" came to this house again!
What have we done to deserve this... that even our last child must be taken from us...
A month ago, our third became a Bi'an as well...
We know... becoming a Bi'an is meant to be an honour... but if we had a choice, we'd rather have our sons here with us...
(At that, the old man can't hold it in any longer. He covers his face with one hand and weeps.)
Sorry, youngster... letting you see an old man cry like a child...
It's all right. Letting it out helps.
Thank you... truly. I do feel a bit steadier now.
(He wipes his face and looks up at you, eyes worn and tired.)
Thank you so much for listening, kiddo. We won't keep you any longer. I'll take the missus out for a little walk... might do her some good.
Okay...
(Old Man Cheng steadies Mrs Cheng, and the two of them drift off into the distance — like withered leaves carried gently on the wind — until they fade from sight.)
I know we shouldn't be this selfish... but it still hurts, no matter how much we tell ourselves otherwise...
Awoo— rrrh— awooo-wooo!

options.content: Good kids don't just go around biting people, you know.
(Best keep my distance... who knows if he's carrying something.)

talks.content: Nah-uh! I'm training so I can be a Bi'an!

options.content: You... you're not a Loongscion, are you? Earthborns can't become Bi'an.

talks.content: There's an old saying in Huaxu: if you put your heart into something, it'll pay off! Lord Argent can see how hard I'm training — he definitely won't turn me away!
When I become a proper, mighty Bi'an, I'll patrol all of Mistwharf every day and catch every bad guy! Just thinking about it gets me all fired up!
...Wow, you're not telling me off like the other grown-ups. You must be a good person. Come on, I'll show you how my training's going!
First off — if you want to fight bad guys as a Bi'an, you need strong muscles. Look! How do mine look?
(He tries to flex, but you can only spot the slightest little bump under his shirt.)
I—I'm still growing! I'll have muscles one day! Besides, most of my training's for agility — watch this!
(He suddenly drops forward and scampers off on hands and feet, kicking up a cloud of dust.)
Cough— cough.
Well? That's my special move — Bi'an Riding the Wind! I look the part, right?

options.content: Mm... so fast you're almost a blur.
Ahaha— ahem. I... just thought of something funny, sorry.

talks.content: Hmph! And I've been practising the Bi'an's roar as well. Awoo—!
(He suddenly lets out a long howl — so that's what he was doing on the ground earlier.)
Awooo... awoooo...
Well...
Awo... awooooo...
(He's completely absorbed in his howling and won't respond to you at all. In the end, you slip away quietly — probably best to give the little "Bi'an" some space.)
Awoo— Well? Sounded just like a real Bi'an, didn't it?
Urgh— urgh... n—no more... I really can't take another mouthful...
Phew... you gave me a fright — thought you were a Starweaver.

options.content: Starweaver...? Did they force you to eat something?
Hello. I'm a Starweaver from Hyperborea.

talks.content: No no, all by my own choice...
Ugh... anything you want — except having dinner with me!
So what's going on here?
I'm Sammy — a merchant from Khemet. I came to Huaxu with the Starweavers.
I was meant to be discussing incense trade with them, but after more than a week in Mistwharf, I've barely touched any business — it's just been meals. Every. Single. Day.
People in Huaxu are far too obsessed with food! Open your eyes in the morning — a huge breakfast. Then a pot of tea that somehow drifts straight into lunch.
After lunch I think, "Finally, a break" — but no, someone appears with a huge tray of pastries and fruit. Finish that, and it's supper already.
After supper, just when I'm ready for bed, someone knocks again — dragging me out for late-night bites.
Urgh... just thinking about it makes me retch...
Why didn't you just say you were full?

At first I couldn't bring myself to say it — didn't want to offend Huaxu's Starweavers. After throwing up a few times, I just couldn't take it anymore, so I finally worked up the courage to tell them I was full. And then... something worse happened...
The Starweavers instantly started piling more food into my bowl — "nutritious", "go on, help yourself", that sort of thing... and I ended up eating three extra bowls!
Urk... I can't— I need to go and be sick again... Huaxu's hospitality is just too much for me to handle... urgh...
Urk... huff... huff...
Grab your gear. We're moving.
(No sooner have you stepped into the black market than a crowd spills out.)
(A black marketeer lies behind them, barely clinging to life. A closer look — it's the very man who doctored a loan contract to trick an innocent girl, then cheated in a duel with her.)

options.content: You lot — arming yourselves to stir up trouble!?
(They're not after you. Best keep out of their way.)
Well, haven't seen him for a few days — look at him now.

talks.content: Ah — Mr Qiu's honoured guest. Forgive me for not offering a proper greeting.
(The leader dips his head — a courtesy entirely out of place in the black market.)
Since you've crossed paths with us, I'd best be clear — save you from any misunderstanding.
(Seeing the doubt in your eyes, Li Shi nods towards the man lying on the ground.)
Not long ago he took a heavy loss in a deal. In the quarrel that followed, he lost his temper and lashed out — so he drew a Bi'an's punishment, and ended up half-dead like this.

options.content: So... you're bringing your men to take revenge?

talks.content: Heh. The black market doesn't take revenge for anyone. You place your stake, you shoulder the consequences — Mr Qiu's rule. So the man swallows that bitter pill himself.
Lose, and you bear the cost yourself. Whether you survive, and what you choose to do afterwards — that's no one else's concern.
I thought you lot were the radical sort.
Many hold that same mistaken view. But the black market is, at its core, only loosely bound.
Those who remain here are the ones who answer to no outside rules — and can afford the cost of that freedom.

We're not afraid of losing. You take the blow, you get back up. What we can't stand are the sore losers — bold and swaggering when things go their way, then crying for protection the moment they don't. There's no room for that sort of weakness here.
So, I trust you see what I'm saying — we're not out to avenge anyone.
As for what we are doing... with the Scourge of Zhuyin ebbing, we're heading into the shadows it leaves behind — to take whatever profit's there. Nothing more.
(He moves off with his men, but after only a few steps he pauses and glances back.)
Since you're Mr Qiu's guest, here's a piece of advice — free of charge.
Some things belong to no one. Those with the strength to claim them... may. Keep your eyes open — you might spot something worthwhile in Mistwharf. Farewell.
My apologies for not greeting you properly. What brings you to the market today?
Mmm — rough on the first whiff, smooth on the finish... now that's proper EverSpring incense.
(He lifts the sticks to his nose, inhales sharply, and savours the scent with unrestrained delight.)
Ahhh~ That hits the spot! Pure as they come.

options.content: (He's clearly not quite right. Best not get involved.)
There's something seriously wrong with you — I'm reporting you to the Magistrates of Yingtian.

talks.content: Oi, what an odd youngster you are. You meet Huaxu's famed incense master — me — and instead of offering respect, you carry on like that. Terribly uncouth.

options.content: That's exactly what a swindler would say.

talks.content: Now, now — let's set a few things straight.
Most people burn incense just to go through the motions, never realising the incense itself is an art.
Take these EverSpring sticks, for instance... hold on, another sniff...
Mmm~ That's got to be Emerald Sandalwood from around Starwharf, with a touch of Azure Mugwort and a bit of Dewgrass in the mix.
Mistwharf's been Huaxu's harbour since forever. The waters here nurture people — and plants — like nowhere else. EverSpring incense uses whatever grows nearby. Brilliant work, truly.
Go on, have a sniff. Feel that rough, prickly bite in the wood?
No.
Right then. Try this one from Haojing — notice anything different?
(He pulls out another stick, lights it, and offers it to you.)
Still nothing.
Haojing sits cradled by mountains. Incense-makers there work with whatever the hills provide, so their sticks always open with a hint of bitterness.
But just after the bitter comes a whisper of sweetness — like the slog of climbing a mountain, wiped clean the moment you reach the summit.
Stand on Haojing's peaks one day and you'll know exactly what I'm talking about.
(Suddenly, he turns his head and sharply inhales towards the distance.)
Mmm... there's a unique scent over that way...
Right, enough chatter. More scents to chase. If fate's willing, we'll meet again~
(With that, he darts off. Even from afar, you can still hear his ecstatic "Ahhh~ That hits the spot!" echoing down the road.)
Now, be a good boy and let our guest have the bigger one.
Heh-heh-heh... you'll all pay for this... every last one of you...
Huh!?
H—How much did you hear!?
Enough to know you're plotting something dodgy.
Nah-uh — it's revenge!
Revenge? For what? And on whom?
Our caravan's suppliers! Working with them is enough to make anyone lose their mind!

options.content: Work always has its headaches. Don't let it eat you up — try to take it easy.
If they're mistreating you, shouldn't the Nine Chapters of Dafeng deal with them?

talks.content: You've no idea — those people are slippery as eels!
At first it's all "we trust your abilities", "let the most capable take the lead" — and somehow we end up doing all the hard bits.
And the moment something goes wrong, suddenly it's "we're all in this together", "we rely on each other" — and they dump the whole mess back on us to fix.
If you refuse, they start dragging their feet — obviously on purpose — but there's no way to prove it...
Ask them outright and they switch to "oh we're so sorry", "it won't happen again, promise" — utter rubbish! It drives me up the wall!
Why not just work with someone else?
I'd love to... but the stuff we deal in is rare. They're the only ones who can get hold of it.
Still, I'm not putting up with it! I've already started drafting my revenge plan — once I'm done, those old geezers will be begging on their knees. Heh-heh...
And what exactly are you planning?
Oh, loads! Let me read you a few:
First — shave a bit off one of their desk legs so the whole thing wobbles!
Second — slip some laxatives into their tea so they can't make it to work!
Third — pour boiling water into the pot of their wealth plants, so their luck dries up and they start losing money!
...None of that sounds particularly harmful. And I'm pretty sure the Nine Chapters forbid things like that.
I know! Why do you think I haven't done any of it yet? Anyway, it's only a draft.
As the old saying goes: "Diligence makes up for dull wits"! If I write down enough ideas, I'm bound to think of a revenge plan that slips past the Nine Chapters!
Look — I've already filled this much!
(She flips through the notebook. The writing is pressed so hard the ink has bled straight through the pages. By your guess, there must be seventy or eighty of them.)
That's... a lot. How long have you been at this?
Erm... the autumn before last? Or maybe the year before that... I can't quite remember.
...Isn't that a rather long timetable for revenge?
They say revenge is a dish best served cold!
At this rate they'll go out of business before you get round to doing anything.
How did you know!?
The last supplier who pushed me around shut down halfway through my revenge plan!
So your real plan is... just outlasting them?
What else can I do? I'm not very clever — I just have to keep at it. As the old saying goes: "Slow and steady wins the race." So I'll just keep writing!

options.content: You could ask Zhiliu for help.
If it helps you feel better, then it might be worth doing.
I do offer revenge-for-hire, you know.

talks.content: P—Proprietress Zhiliu!? No, no — absolutely not... She's far too busy to listen to me whinge...
Thanks! Are people from outside Huaxu all this nice?
No, no — I can't have someone risking their life on my account.
I know her. She's very kind — and she really does care about traders like you.
My friends just laugh at me — say I'm deluding myself. And... honestly, I know that too. I just can't think of anything else to do.
*sign*... Anyway, thanks for listening to me ramble.
Really...? Then... I'll think about it... Maybe practise what to say first...
Talking to you's really helped... I think I can write two more pages today!
Just don't spend another three years rehearsing it this time.
(She picks up her pen and starts scribbling once more, muttering new revenge ideas under her breath.)
I've got it! I'll put chilli powder in their pillows... heehee...
Good {性别：sir|lady}, pray wait a moment — I have a favour to ask.
Could you help me catch a few small animals?
Small animals...? What exactly are you planning?
Rest assured, good {性别：sir|lady} — I've no wish to harm a single living creature. I'm to perform on the zither here today, and hoped the little animals might be my audience.
Why animals, specifically?
Perhaps you've not heard — in ancient Huaxu there lived a zither-master celebrated across the land. It's said that when she performed, even wild beasts would stop and listen.
It has long been my aspiration to reach such heights!
But the little creatures around Mistwharf are dreadfully timid. I had barely sat down — hadn't so much as touched the strings — before they all fled.
So I've never once had the chance to let them hear the piece I composed with such devotion. A pity... truly a pity.
If you could bring them here and help me realise this wish, I'd be deeply grateful — and of course, you shall be handsomely rewarded.

options.content: All right then — I'll see what I can do.

talks.content: After giving it some thought, you decide to attract them with food.
Soon enough, a few birds and a deer follow the scent and draw near to Ju Mu.
What a clever idea — truly ingenious, good {性别：sir|lady}! Your reward is prepared; please, accept it.
I shall begin at once. If you've the leisure, you are most welcome to stay and listen.
(Ju Mu settles himself with great ceremony, rolls up his sleeves, raises his hands — and begins to play...)
(...And at last you discover the source of that strange noise from earlier.)
Cheep!?
Brrh—!!
(The animals scatter at once, abandoning their food mid-bite.)

options.content: Looks like you've got a lot more practising to do.
You should be paying me for sitting through that.
Good heavens — you played so well the animals are all fired up!

talks.content: H—How could this happen...? Why would it turn out like this...?
Are you sure that even counts as music?
A piece meant to transcend the ordinary naturally sounds different from common tunes.

As it was meant to delight even animals, I thought it best to draw inspiration from nature. For instance, the piece I played included the snap of breaking branches, the buzz of insects' wings, and the sound of stray dogs scratching at the ground...
I truly believed I'd poured my heart into a flawless composition... Never did I imagine all that effort would amount to nothing...

options.content: Is it possible that the sounds you chose are just... not very pleasant to begin with?

talks.content: Good {性别：sir|lady}, you have enlightened me — with a single remark!

I see... the choice of sounds was at fault. I must go home and start afresh! Let me think... the cawing of crows, the gnawing of field mice, the scrape of metal on stone... yes, that should do nicely!

True enough! I'm only asking for a small donation out of goodwill — no one's twisting arms here. Just seeing whether anyone's kind enough to help a thirsty storyteller — one favoured by Lord Argent — wet his throat.
Many thanks, traveller — I'll remember the kindness.
(A few generous onlookers toss over some silver coins. Before long, a tea-seller trots up with a clay pot. Quan Doutong snatches it up, takes a long, satisfied gulp, wipes his mouth, and carries on.)

Where's the busiest place in all Huaxu? Haojing, of course — and that's where our story begins. Tucked away in one of its narrow little lanes lived two households: the Lyus on one side, the Mas on the other.

They usually rubbed along well enough — polite, neighbourly, never a harsh word. But then the Ministry of Fortune announced that, with so many old houses falling into disrepair, they were organising restoration works — which meant every household now had to report the size of its property.

And that, dear guests, is where things took a turn. The larger the area you reported, the more silver the Ministry would hand out for repairs. So both families — without comparing notes — began thinking the same thought: "What if we just stretched the numbers a touch?"
The snag was that the strip of ground in the lane belonged to no one — not a single record said whose it was. And just like that, they were at a standstill.
The Lyus said, "Our pear tree throws its shade over the lane — so the land must be ours!"
The Mas shot back, "We've dried our spices there for years, and you never complained! That makes it ours!"
Soon enough they were bickering loud enough to shake the roof tiles loose. If not for the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, they'd have been rolling on the ground wrestling like street dogs.
Each side had its reasons — so how could the dispute be settled?
(He pauses dramatically, milking the moment.)
Now, remember — this is Haojing, a city full of folk who make their living sorting out neighbourly quarrels.
So one such mediator caught wind of the fuss and hurried over at once. He hears them out, smiles, and rattles off a verse on the spot:
"The black loong stirs up the worst in men; Lord Argent's wrath checks greed and pain. Rows flare bright then fade in vain — yield three feet, and peace shall remain."

Even Zhuyin was sealed away by Lord Argent for its wickedness — so why should decent folk in fair Huaxu behave with such greed and temper today? Hearing that, both families fell silent. Their faces went red as cooked prawns, and they slunk back home without another word.

To show they truly meant to make peace, the Lyus pulled down their front wall and rebuilt it three feet further in — even set up a little statue of Lord Argent by the gate. The Mas saw that and did exactly the same.
And just like that — harmony restored! In time, that very lane became the place neighbours went whenever a quarrel arose, letting Lord Argent witness their goodwill for themself.
And today, allow me to tweak that verse a touch — like so: "To show that virtue dwells within the heart — yield three feet, and goodwill speaks for itself." What say you, folks?
(The crowd breaks into cheerful applause, praising Lord Argent. A fresh handful of coins slips into Quan Doutong's palms as people wander off in twos and threes.)
If you've got a few coins to spare, toss them in. If not, a bit of applause'll do!

(Clutching the phial to her chest, the girl called Yan dashed off, full of excitement.)
You're a patient one, guest — waiting here all this time. So then, what sort of draught are you after? A tonic for your health? Or, like that girl just now, something to slim the figure?

Those who seek longevity should rest well and eat well. Those who hope for beauty should mind their skin, keep themselves pleasant, and not push too hard. Guest, you're taking the word "medicine" far too rigidly.
Medicine can be a decoction you swallow... but it can just as well be a way of living. It may look as though I'm handing out potions, but really, I'm teaching them how to look after themselves.

One way or another, I'm getting an explanation today!

See those Bi'an patrolling the docks? What we catch, they spot — and what we don't, ha, they still will.

Those Bi'an keep watch day and night to stop anything shady from getting into Huaxu. Their noses? Sharp as can be — one sniff and they'll know exactly who's hiding what.
Good taste, my friend — Huaxu's finest, right here. These Lunarose sachets above all: if you'd seek Lord Argent's favour, you'll want one.

Souvenirs for travellers! First time in Huaxu? Don't pass me by — sachets, folding fans, curios, trinkets, all the little treasures you could want!
