That's all I needed to know. See you.

talks.content: Of course! Here — this hanging scroll, every verse of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng laid out clear as day. Take it home, and you'll have the perfect piece to show your friends.
Wouldn't dream of it! I've been at this stall for nearly ten years — folk round here know I give a fair deal. Ask around if you like.

options.content: That's all I needed to know. See you.

talks.content: Take care! Pop by again — sure to be something you'll fancy.
And take a look at our Huaxu exclusives — traditional pieces, well loved by both young and old.
If you fancy something a bit different, we've insect-motif pieces too — just the thing for a unique taste.
Oh, and don't miss our new scented candles: a breath of Huaxu in each — travellers from abroad always come back for more!

options.content: Not my thing. Anything more practical — something for day-to-day use?
I want the lot, but I've no money — could I have them on tick?

talks.content: Ah, dear guest, I'm but a peddler of souvenirs. Such things are for delight and remembrance, not for use.
AAh... sorry, no can do for a small stall like mine. But if you're looking to earn a bit of coin, I can put in a word with the Starweavers down at the docks — they're always hiring porters.

options.content: That's all I needed to know. See you.

talks.content: Guests from abroad — travellers and traders alike — carry a token home for those left behind. As for things of real use... truth be told, our everyday wares seldom suit their habits.
And if something were truly needed, the Starweavers would've made it common long ago — sold everywhere. It wouldn't be a Huaxu exclusive.

options.content: That's all I needed to know. See you.

talks.content: You lot might not know this, but this humble wharf of ours wasn't always so quiet. A thousand years ago, a great man once set sail from right here!
And who was that great man, you ask? You all know his name — Ju, co-founder of the Nine Chapters, and the forefather of the Jishu Sect!

Folks, lend me your ears for a moment — let me tell you the thousand-year tale of our very own Starwharf! Just as trade should be fair and square, so too should our past — plain and open for all to see.
(Behind you, Old Man Liu's voice carries on — still praising Huaxu's two founders as the onlookers clap along...)

Before the Nine Chapters came to guard us, old Huaxu was a hard place to live. Back then, the Filthoids ran wild, feasting on the helpless. To stay alive, every man, woman, and child had to fight or flee — no exceptions.

And where there's strife, there are graves. People dwindled, babies rarely saw their first spring. Even the proud Loongscions were at their wits' end, searching high and low for a way to bring peace back to the land.

Among them was Ju. He roamed every corner of Huaxu, seeking peace and finding none. At last, he thought: If peace can't be found on our shores, maybe it lies beyond the sea — in what others know, in what we've yet to learn.

Back in those days, there were no great ships — not a single Starweaver to be seen. To set sail was a pure gamble: with luck, you might wash ashore on some lonely isle, counting seabirds to pass the days; without it, you'd be fish food at the bottom of the sea.
But Ju, bent on peace for all, built a boat with his own hands — asking help from no one — and pushed off alone from this very Starwharf!

By Lord Argent's grace, Ju braved every storm the sea could throw at him, till at last he reached a hidden land where a sacred tower rose into the clouds. But peace? Not a trace of it there, either. So he turned his prow homeward once more — and with him came others who, like him, longed for peace.

Seasons passed, years slipped away... and folks here thought Ju had long been claimed by the sea. Then one day — from the horizon he came sailing back, right into Starwharf's arms, a handful of weary souls at his side.
You might be wondering — how did Ju find his way across that endless sea? Was it the gods who guided him? Or sheer guts and blind faith?
Neither! All right, I won't keep you guessing — you know that Stellapass the Starweavers use to find their way at sea? Well, Ju's was the very first — built with his own hands.
With plain old planks, he charted the stars, found his bearings, and sailed wherever his heart pleased.

It was Ju's voyage — out into the unknown and back again — that freed the Loongscions of Huaxu from their fear of the sea. For Starwharf's prosperity and the Starweavers' success today, we owe our thanks to Ju — the first soul brave enough to face the waves.

And remember this, folks — Ju and Yang, founders side by side, names we must never let fade. Without them, there'd be no Huaxu as we know it today. So keep their names close, keep their deeds alive — and pass them on!
(The crowd bursts into cheers.)
The Stellapass is running fine. Come to think of it, it's about due for its next maintenance...

It's been less than three years since we installed this Stellapass. Why does it need maintenance already? I just hope they remembered to call in a craftsman from the Jishu Sect... Better check whether the calibration marks have faded.
Whoa! You scared me! You're not from around here, are you? What are you doing on our ship?
Me? I'm just checking the ship's Stellapass. I'm the mechanic in charge of its maintenance. Without it, the ship wouldn't be able to leave port.
Oh, I'm in the middle of checking the Stellapass. If anything's off, we won't be able to set sail. Whatever you need, please come back later.
If you need anything, come back later — I still need to check for overheating.
The Stellapass is running fine. Come to think of it, it's about due for its next maintenance...
Hmm, there was a slight scale error, but after five additional calibration runs, the readings are basically correct now. Perhaps we can request to postpone the maintenance.
Oh, it's you again — the visitor from afar. Here to take another look?

options.content: That's all I wanted to ask.

talks.content: Me? I'm the ship's mechanic. I make sure the Stellapass runs smoothly — if it fails, the next voyage will be in trouble.
It's the Starweavers' lifeline — a marvel our ancestors left us. Out on the open sea, it reads the stars and keeps us steady, so we never lose our course.
If you need me, come back later — I've still got readings to take.
I need to log all this down — it'll be useful when we file our report to the Ministry of Fortune.

options.content: That's all I wanted to ask.

talks.content: The seas around Huaxu are wild — without the Stellapass to guide us, we'd be swept off course in no time. That's why we always carry out a full check before every long voyage.

options.content: Where's the Stellapass? I don't see it.

talks.content: Maintenance? It just means having the Jishu Sect masters inspect it, to see if any parts have come loose. Usually it's fine — but out at sea, with all the pitching and rolling, a few bumps are hard to avoid.
Ha! It's right beneath our feet, silly. On ships like this, the Stellapass is built into the hold — only the main plate is turned upward to face the sky, so it can read the stars.
We regular mechanics can identify problems, but we can't repair them. Only the Jishu Sect has the proper tools for that. No need to trouble them too often — once every four or five years is enough.
If I had to put it in your terms, it's a bit like a massive chandelier. Out at sea, there's always someone below keeping watch on how it turns — otherwise, we'd drift off course.
And when we do, we have to bring along our daily readings — it helps them make a proper assessment.
Ms Bai, could you clarify that?
In Huaxu, none may harm another — by any means, for any reason. Should another be hurt because of you, the fault is yours.
Right... so, no shooting anyone. I can manage that.
Good. Since you are in Huaxu, we shall keep the firearms you brought for safekeeping, and return them once you depart.
Fair enough. I'm here to trade, not to fight. I'll follow the local rules — that Dafeng thing. Anything else I should know?
Since you are here for trade, hear the second chapter: "To break faith or betray a vow — this must not be done."
I get "betray a vow", but what does "break faith" mean?
When you trade with our people, once a price is agreed, it must be sealed as a covenant under Lord Argent's witness. Without that, your promise holds no weight here.
Oh, I see — contracts. We do that too. No problem!
Not quite the same. Our covenants are written in ink mixed with Lunarose ash, beneath Lord Argent's gaze. That mark bears the deity's witness.
And should either side break their oath... Bi'an will come for them.
Bi'an? The great hound of Huaxu — I've heard of it!
Mind your tongue! Speak not of Bi'an so lightly!
Mum keeps saying I'll get horns when I'm older. Year before last she said "next year", and last year she said "next year" again... still nothing!
What if they never grow? No — I don't want to be an Earthborn forever. I want to be a proper Loongscion!

options.content: What's wrong with being an Earthborn?
But Loongcions might turn into Filthoids.

talks.content: Uh-uh! Earthborns don't get magic. Only Loongscions do — they're the ones who serve Lord Argent in Huaxu!
Filthoids? I'm not scared! If I ever turned into one, I'd be a mighty Bi'an! Mum would be so proud of me!
How do I make my horns grow? Maybe if I give them a little tug... ow! That hurts!
Oh, it's you, {性别：sir|miss}. Mum taught me a trick: she says if I touch other Loongscions' horns here at the Starwharf, mine will grow too.
She also said mine will grow just like those I touch! So I have to find the Loongscion with the prettiest horns! {性别：Sir|Miss}, I like yours — can I touch them?
Thank you! They're small and hard — let me have a proper feel.
I'll be a Loongscion yet — just you wait and see!
If I grow horns one day, will Mum be happy? Will I get amazing magic too? {性别：Sir|Miss}, can you do magic?

options.content: I can, but I won't be able to use it while I'm in Huaxu.
I can't — I only use a sword and my fists to fight.

talks.content: Oh, I know! You must have super strong magic, right? I bet you could blow up mountains — or send thirty Sable Bi'an flying with just one punch!

Huh? But in Huaxu you're not supposed to be violent! Still... you're so confident. Maybe you're one of those... Yingtian-somethings? Um, I forgot the name — but they're the only ones allowed to fight in Huaxu!
Wow! That sounds amazing! {性别：Sir|Miss}, if my horns grow, will you teach me that magic?
They're amazing! They serve Lord Argent directly. Everyone respects them. Super cool!
Grow them first, then we'll talk.
Do you think... when I grow horns, I could be a Loongscion as awesome as you?
Grow them first, then we'll talk.
If I'd known sooner, I would've joined right away. With EverSpring supporting me, I wouldn't have lost that big deal just for lacking a bit of capital...
Ah, my friend — are you here to apply to become a Starweaver as well?

options.content: Sort of. I just happened to hear you talking about it.
I just happened to hear you talking about it.

talks.content: Then you've found the right person. I just completed the entire process myself — paperwork, proof of capital, every step. I know it inside out.
Oh? I thought most visitors came to EverSpring hoping to become Starweavers. Now that you mention it, the process does differ a bit between locals and outsiders.
Not that it's troublesome — EverSpring never makes things difficult for an honest trader.
Still, don't worry — EverSpring treats every fair and honest merchant equally.
Thanks, but I don't have such plans at the moment.
Thanks, but I don't have such plans at the moment.
I never realized being a Starweaver came with so many perks. EverSpring truly is remarkable.
Ah, my foreign friend — have you decided to join the Starweavers this time?

options.content: You're quite the spokesperson for them, you know.
So not every merchant in Huaxu is a Starweaver, then?

talks.content: If you knew how much support EverSpring gives its Starweavers, you'd be just as enthusiastic as I am.

options.content: Then what sort of benefits are we talking about?

talks.content: No, not at all. Starweavers are one group; there are also hawkers and stallholders — quite a different crowd.
Of course. Come find me when you're ready to apply.
Quite a few, actually. For newcomers like me, once you join, you can apply for a starting fund — there's interest, but it's low — and you can use it for any kind of trade you prefer.

Being a Starweaver certainly has its advantages, but also plenty of rules. Once a deal is made, you must seal a covenant and follow the proper terms. For those used to traveling trade or running small stalls, such rules can feel a bit restrictive.
With EverSpring's name behind us, even the largest merchants treat us with respect — some even approach us first simply because we're Starweavers.
I used to be the same — traveling from place to place, doing small trades along the way. Saved up a little, then came here hoping to make something bigger of it.

options.content: How many Starweavers are there in Huaxu?

talks.content: It's a far cry from the days when I had to go door to door trying to gather stock.
How many? Hard to say. Plenty of shops register just to make their names sound more trustworthy. If I had to guess... perhaps six or seven out of ten.
In any case, it's common to meet Starweavers in all sorts of trades wherever you go.
Mr Cong, this year's building work at EverSpring has already gone well beyond the plan. It was meant to be a modest repair, and now there's even a tea room added.

Yes, I know — Li provided the silver for that. If his gift was accepted, why not mine? We Starweavers earn our living abroad and return home to honour EverSpring — it's been our custom for generations.

We truly cannot, sir. You know how people are — everyone wishes to contribute to EverSpring. The guild was never a grand one to begin with; it's grown brick by brick to what it is now. We can't continue like this forever.
If we keep building at this rate, EverSpring will wear itself thin — and we'll all end up rebuilding in the end.
I don't care. You've taken Li's silver, you'll take mine as well. If not, I'll come by in the dead of night and leave the money here myself.
Well... Mr Li has been waiting since the year before last for this year's building quota. He put in his request the moment it opened — there is, after all, an order of precedence.
Then use my silver to help the new Starweavers — just as the guild once lent its hand to me.
I'm not sure. But the Starweavers made this moon, piece by piece — there must be a way up!
And it's like a huge incense burner for our city! Someone's got to climb up and clean it once in a while.
Yes, but where's the way up? I can't see anything!
Shh, I'm thinking! I'll figure something out!

options.content: What are you two talking about?
Why do you want to climb it?

talks.content: Whoa! A foreigner!?
Someone said the very top's the highest place in Mistwharf! You can see the whole Mistwharf from up there. We just want to have a look!
See you, traveller! Come on, let's get back to figuring out how to climb it!
Do you like the big moon too?
Uh-huh! We want to count all the Chipgulls that fly over EverSpring in one day!

options.content: So it's not real? People built it?

talks.content: Silly Bunny! Everyone likes it! It's so big you can even see it from the sea!
What? Really? It's so bright and huge! How can you not like it? You must be fibbing!
You didn't know? Oh, right — you're not from here! The moon's actually a giant incense burner in Mistwharf. A really rich Starweaver paid to have it built!

options.content: Why did they make it look like a moon?

talks.content: Oh, I know this one! The Starweaver said people who sail away are like stars in the sky — they'll all come home one day! So home needs a bright moon to guide them back!
Aren't you a know-it-all! Then do you know what the Starweaver called it?
Erm... I forgot...
Ahem! Let me tell you then — it's called... Homeward Bright Moon!
That's such a long name! No wonder I forgot. "Big Moon" sounds much better!
Didn't expect to stumble upon something this old today. It seems barely stable enough to read the weather, let alone fortunes...
It must date back to my great-great-grandfather's time — or perhaps even earlier. Well, you get the idea. It's ancient.
Me? I happened upon this old Stellapass and thought I'd keep it as a curio. And you? Are you interested in relics as well?
Ah, a traveller with a taste for Huaxu craftsmanship. Then allow me to play the host — ask away, and I'll share what I know.
Ah... this Stellapass — now that's a piece of history!
There you are. You wished to learn about the Stellapass, did you not?
Reciting it by rote won't help. Use your head — you must understand it, or it will never stay with you.
Easy for you to say. I can hardly read, and that sheet's packed full of words. I can't make sense of them.
Packed? The Starweavers' maxims run to only seven lines. The Nine Chapters of Dafeng have nine!
Well, I've not memorised the Nine Chapters either...

options.content: What are you two talking about?

talks.content: Ah, you're a traveller, aren't you? Pardon the scene. My friend here's just joined the Starweavers — I'm teaching him our trade maxims.
Fulong, where do you think you're going? Back here! Keep reciting!
If they hadn't asked about them when we joined, I'd never have learnt a word. I trade fair and square — that should be proof enough, without all this fuss.
Nooooooo!!
Enough talk. Recite!

options.content: I'm curious about the maxims as well — what are they, exactly?

talks.content: You are? Very well then — one more listener won't hurt. You can both listen in.
There are seven in all. They go as follows:
Count not profit but righteousness as honour;
Count not splendour but virtue as nobility;
Count not cheapness but quality as value;
Count not cunning but honesty as skill;
Count not rarity but fitness as treasure;
Count not hoarding but kindness as wealth;
Count not rhetoric but truth as measure.
By Lord Argent — how did you remember every word? You've got second sight, seeing the text clear through the page?
Not everyone's as slow as you! Traveller, was there any line you didn't quite catch? I can explain it if you wish.
Good day. I'm the enquiries clerk for EverSpring. Should you have any questions about the guild or the Starweavers, please don't hesitate to ask.
Of course. What would you like to know? Is it about EverSpring and the Starweavers, the services we provide here, or something else?
Take care, and do visit again if you have further questions.
Long, it's been a while. Care to try the new Silver Needle? The fragrance is exquisite~
Still in the mood for tea, are you? Haven't you heard? A batch of Loong Qiqi incense has just appeared in Haojing — no one knows its source — and the price's shot through the roof!
It's always been expensive, yes, but this? Five, six times the usual rate! Someone's clearly manipulating the market, driving it up on purpose.
Easy there, Long — no need to blow your top. It's nothing worth losing sleep over.

Nothing, you say? Every shipment of rare incense in Haojing passes through me! My own batch of Loong Qiqi hasn't even arrived, and suddenly another turns up from nowhere — now my regular clients are demanding answers!
So you rushed all the way to EverSpring overnight? Come now, catch your breath — sit and have some tea first.
You sly old fox, Chawen — what are you plotting this time? Don't tell me you've a hand in that mysterious batch yourself!
Now, now — how could I be to blame? I'm merely saying that fretting won't help. Report it to EverSpring, and they'll handle the matter properly.
Explain everything to the higher-ups. Before long, Haojing will have more Loong Qiqi incense in supply, and the price will settle of its own accord, will it not?
You mean to say... EverSpring will intervene? And what would they gain from that?
Stability, of course. With prices like these, incense ceases to be used as incense — it becomes a game of hot potato. Keep this up and someone's bound to get burned.
So EverSpring will no doubt release another batch soon, just enough to cool the market down.
Hmph... I've never seen the like. They'd best act quickly.

Come now, Long, sit and rest a while. There's no cause for such agitation. I've been with EverSpring for decades — I've seen this sort of trick more times than I can count. Here, let me pour you some tea.
The Borealberry jam that came in yesterday — why is it still held up in inspection? I need my goods, and I need them now!
Please, Mr Smith, do calm yourself. I'll look into the matter straightaway.
Let me see... three shipments of Borealberry jam from Hyperborea — yes, they did arrive yesterday. But it appears there's been a small mix-up. We're still checking everything over.
My bakery goes through barrels of the stuff every single day! The order was late to begin with, and now I'm nearly out — by the time your inspection's finished, I'll have no customers left!
What's there to check, anyway? It's jam, not contraband! They didn't even bother inspecting it back in Hyperborea!
Please, Mr Smith — just to confirm. Of your three ships carrying Borealberry jam, were two fully loaded and one only half?
Certainly not! All three were full — I watched the dockhands load every barrel myself!
And that, I'm afraid, is where the problem lies. When the ships arrived, our tally clerk noted that one hull was riding noticeably higher than the others. That's far beyond normal wastage.
You mean to say... someone stole my jam en route?
We can't say for certain just yet. The Ministry of Fortune has already instructed all three captains to hand in their logbooks. We should have the truth by tomorrow.
All right then... could you take me down to the docks? Even seeing the barrels — from a distance, at least — would set my mind at ease.
Of course. Though the shipment has already been moved to EverSpring's warehouse. Come, I'll escort you there myself.
No matter how far I wander, I always end up here again. What is this place? Who... who am I?
A Wishen...? Yes... I remember now. Born for no reason... left to wander without purpose. But still, I long to go home... Can you tell me... where that is?
Lord Argent...? No... that's not me. Lord Argent watches over Huaxu. I'm only... a Wishen.
I don't know where your home is... but I don't think it's here.
Who are you...? Could you tell me... where my home might be?
Is that so... and yet... I always find myself back here... Home... where could it be...
Home... but where is it? And where am I...?
You've come back... breathe in... do you feel it? The air... there's a scent — faint, but unlike any other...
Strange... but it's there — like candles at home, once they've burnt away... A warmth that pricks faintly, yet feels gentle and comforting... almost intoxicating.

options.content: Maybe it's just the incense from those who come to pay their respects.
As far as I know, leaves don't turn into Wishen.

talks.content: Right? That scent — like candles at home, once they've burnt away... A warmth that pricks faintly, yet feels gentle and comforting... almost intoxicating.
You wouldn't understand... that feeling of finally going home...
No... not that. The incense of mourning carries sorrow and yearning, but never the scent of home. I've wandered so far, so many times... yet this fragrance always pulls me back.
Perhaps you're right... Then what am I... some soil... the air itself... a pebble by the path... Mmm... it feels so warm here... maybe I'll just stay...
That's why I always come back. No matter how far I go, I return. Tell me — could this be my home? Why else would I feel... so at peace...?

options.content: Any way you look at it, this place doesn't feel like a home.

talks.content: Tell me... could this be my home? When I was alive... did I live upon this tree? Could I have been... a leaf?
But I can feel it... I'm connected to everything here. We share one breath — breathe in... the warmth wrapping around us... pulling me back... Ah... I'm going home...
Maybe... maybe I really was a leaf once... yes... that's why it feels so familiar... This is it — this is my home. I'm a Wishen... born of a leaf!

O merciful light of Lord Argent, shine through the shadowed bourne; let lone souls and lingering shades not wander, nor remain forlorn. Let the woes of yore be laid aside; this day be ferried across, bathed in kindly light.
Greetings, traveller. A deliverance prayer — verses passed down through the Wuqiongzang Sect, to guide the Wishen here to peace.
By vow and decree we summon the lost: Cease your wandering; hasten unto the Realm of Bliss...
Ah, it's you. Would you lend your voice, and chant with me?

options.content: Could you recite the whole prayer?
What brings you to chant it?

talks.content: Of course. It would be better still if you joined me.
My father... he passed away last year. Now it's only my mother and me. Whenever I miss him, I come here to recite a prayer or two.
By vow and decree we summon the lost: Cease your wandering; hasten unto the Realm of Bliss...
O merciful light of Lord Argent, shine through the shadowed bourne; let lone souls and lingering shades not wander, nor remain forlorn.
Perhaps it does, perhaps not. For me, it's a small solace. When I was little, I always thought Father worked too hard. I used to tell myself — once I was grown, I'd let him live in ease and peace.
Have you heard the tale of Huaxu's Wishen? They are spirits bound by unfinished business, unable to move on. If Father still can't let us go... he might have become one too.
Let the woes of yore be laid aside; this day be ferried across, bathed in kindly light.
But before I could shoulder the family myself, he was already gone... So I come here and pray, hoping he's at peace, somewhere beyond my reach...
Perhaps... perhaps he'll come here too, one day...

options.content: What makes you think your father would come here?
If he could see you now, he'd rest easy.

talks.content: O spirits wronged and untimely dead, let every knot be loosed; all bonds and clinging longings — unbind, and fade with the light.

I cannot say... it's only a feeling. If he isn't here, then let this prayer be for the other Wishen still bound to this world. And if they cross paths on that unseen shore... please... tell my father of me.
Then... may this prayer reach the other Wishen still bound to this world. And if they cross paths on that unseen shore... please... tell my father of me.
The Bagua guideth the way; at the Gate of Water the path of blessing openeth. Pass onward to the gentle bourne — in quiet, safe and sound.
In lives to come, rise or fall as thy heart inclineth; sow thine own good fortune, and its fruit shall long endure.
By writ and vow we charge the dead: cast off the cloud of doubt; swift as the edict bids, depart to blissful fields.
Oh, Grandpa, you're being silly again! Not on the ground, not in the water — on my head! Hmm... if that's too hard, my shoulder's okay too!

options.content: Were you talking to a Wishen?

talks.content: Huh? Talking to myself? Maybe! But you spoke to me first — so now I'm talking to you!
Nope! Just me talking to me! But then you said something — so now I'm talking to you!
Then who were you really talking to?
You don't know where you are, do you, traveller from far away? It's scary here! Really scary! All the Loongcions and Earthborn who die in Huaxu — they all turn into Wishen and come here!
Well? Are you scared? If you are... you'd better run quick!
Grandpa! If you're really back, make a leaf fall on my head!
Hey! You really came back? Not even a little bit scared?

options.content: The Wishen won't hurt me. So why would I be afraid?
I hope you'll get to see your grandpa.

talks.content: Me too! But some travellers I met before — when they heard the dead turn into Wishen here, they just screamed and ran away!
I will! Grandpa's definitely coming back to stay with me.
They don't know the Wishen don't hurt anyone. They just stay here... really quiet...

options.content: So what are you doing here?

talks.content: Grandpa got really sick — he said it was something called "ageing". Then Lord Argent came and took him away. Before he went to sleep, he told me he once saw, at Twilight Ravine, people who died turning into Wishen.
He said maybe he'd turn into one too — then he could stay with me forever.
I waited and waited at home, but Grandpa never came back. Then Mum said the Wishen only live here... so I came to find him.

options.content: But it's so spooky here. Aren't you scared?

talks.content: Mum says we can't see the Wishen. So I told Grandpa — if he can hear me, drop a leaf on my head! But Grandpa's so silly... he still hasn't done it...
I was, at first. So I started talking to Grandpa. Then I thought... even if there are other Wishen here, they were people once too, right?

People who die still have family. And when there's family, someone's always missing them. Like me and Grandpa — even if he's gone, we still remember him. When I think about that... I'm not scared anymore.
Hmm... I wonder how long this tree has been standing here.
I asked Fang — he said it was already here when he got here. Jie said the same. But they've both been gone for ages now... So when did this tree start growing?
Hi there! Did you come to see the big tree too?
Heehee, I knew it! I told Fang and Jie people would be curious about it — but they just laughed! And look, someone really came!
Huh? You don't like trees? But this one's special! It's not like any of the others!
Bye-bye! Next time you come back, let's talk about the tree again!
Oh well... if you don't like it, that's fine. I'll just keep thinking about the tree. You can go talk to someone else!
I can hear it — the breath of all things: the whisper of leaves, the murmur beneath the soil, the drip of water. I can hear... everything.
Do you hear it? The tree — it keeps talking. None of them can hear... no one but me... only me.
Of course they do! You just don't listen — your ears are sealed shut! Be still. Feel it. Listen... there! It's speaking again — it's saying...
Hush... its voice... so faint... I can't quite catch it. Just a bit more time... just a little more...
This tree! It keeps talking!
I hear it! Louder than before! You — were you drawn here by the leaves as well? Tell me — did you hear it too!?

options.content: (...I'd better stay away from this lunatic.)

talks.content: No! Listen closely — beneath the rustle there's another sound, a whisper of its own. It's speaking again... calling to me!
I knew it — you're not like the others! What did it say? Tell me, quickly!
You'll come back... on the day the tree foretold.
Grow... yes. From a tiny seed to what it's become. Like you — walking from far away, each step taking root, a path growing a journey.

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Blossom... yes. A tree lives long, yet its flowering is brief — that's why every eye is drawn to it. People are the same: pulled by unseen seasons, and then — they bloom, sudden and bright. Even Lord Argent would pause to marvel.

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Decay... ha... Do trees mourn their own decay? When they fall, new life stirs beneath. Yet... that's my thought, not the tree's. To it, decay isn't sorrow at all...
The tree... it keeps repeating one line...
Hmph. You'll never understand — neither me, nor the tree. It doesn't matter. The tree has already told me... everything.
In the end, I've learnt this: everyone hears a different voice. The tree speaks what lies hidden in our hearts — and now it's calling my name...
It says... what has withered shall bloom again, what is lost shall return.
But beyond my name... I heard its own voice too. It's telling us...

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Do you know where we are? Every time my head clears, I end up back here. The clay idol on the offering table — its face all cracked, like the wall back home.
Home...? Can't call it to mind either. I only remember incense in the air — not this musty kind, but sweet, like sugar frosting. Did you have sweets where you're from?

I don't remember sweets, but we had a river — so wide you'd never see the far bank. In summer, people cast their nets, and the fish came up shining. One slap of its tail — and I'd be soaked all over. Ever seen fish that glow?
No... but I've seen a great wooden wheel, taller than this tree. When it turned, it hummed softly, lifting water up to the fields.
Once it jammed — lots of people gathered, knocking and tapping. I squeezed in for a look... and got a face full of mud. Heh... did you get mud on yours too?
How would a Wishen get mud on his face? Just the wind. Tell me — why are we here? I've walked off plenty of times, and always ended up back again.
Yesterday I walked east. Saw a field of wheat, all gold. I crouched to touch a handful — but the moment I reached out, I was back here again.
I want to go home... Tell me, where is our home, really?
Don't know... But wherever it is, it's surely not here.
Right... definitely not here.
Hey, you there! What are you gawping at? Yes, you. Don't look like you belong here... and sure as hell not one of the regulars. So, what brings you here, then?
Oho, got some bite, have you? This isn't a playground for brats like you. Only legends like me — hic! — the great Chizhatian — get to walk these streets, you hear?
Hey, I'm being nice here, you know! You don't even know the half of it — long ago, monsters called the Jiao haunted these parts. Man-eating beasts. Their favourite snack? Fresh-faced cubs like you!
You'd better start begging me to watch your back — hic! — or the Jiao will swallow you whole.
Heh, lucky you ran into me. Tell you what — buy me a fine pot of wine — hic! — and I'll make sure you get out of Haze Market in one piece. Deal?
You're drunk.
Me? Drunk? Nah — hic! — not me! Come here, I'll tell you all about the... hic!... the Jiao... hic!
Oi, kid — Haze Market isn't the sort of place you just stroll into for fun.
You again, eh? Hah... you don't often see the same bright-eyed youngster twice in this place. Back so soon? Not scared the Jiao will gobble you up?
(He seems a touch more sober this time...)

options.content: So what exactly are the Jiao, then...?

talks.content: Oh, curious now, are you? And here I was thinking Miss Zhiliu's honoured guest would've heard a few of Haze Market's tales already.
Oho, fiery little thing, aren't you? The last one who talked to me like that — hah, I threw him to the Jiao!
You knew who I was all along? Then why pick a fight with me on purpose last time?
But I know who you are — Mr Qiu's aide, Miss Zhiliu's honoured guest. So I'll be generous and let you walk away in one piece.

options.content: So what exactly are the Jiao, then...?

talks.content: Ha! That's the fun of it. Like I said — not many fresh faces like yours turn up round here. So — fancy hearing my tale of the Jiao? Buy me a pot of wine and I'll tell you.

options.content: Make it a good one, and I might.

talks.content: Heh-heh, knew you'd bite. In Huaxu's old lore, they say when the Loongscions fall under the Dark Loong's spell, they become dreadful creatures — the Jiao.
Tch... no fun at all, are you? I took you for a livelier sort than those coin-counting traders. Never mind — I'll just have to find some bargeman to fetch me a pot of wine instead.

The Jiao have no voices of their own, and they fear the light. They dwell in damp, shadowed caverns, feeding on the flesh of men. To draw their prey closer, they steal other voices — singing from deep within the dark.
Those who hear that hauntingly beautiful song draw closer, curious... and end up in the Jiao's belly. Now then — where do you think they gather most often?
Don't tell me... the cavern outside Haze Market?
Ha! Sharp little thing, aren't you! That's right — the Tidesong Cavern itself!
Are there still Jiao around these days?
No, not these days — no need for creatures like that anymore.
What's that supposed to mean?
It means what it means. Wouldn't be half as fun if I told you outright, eh? You're a sharp one — go on then, have a guess.
Why do you think no one's seen a real Jiao in years — only stories left behind? And why has the Tidesong Cavern fallen silent ever since Mr Qiu came?
Let's see... old cotton, bit of tung oil — pack it in tight. Two thin planks either side, nail 'em firm... aye, that'll hold her.
Kiddo, do me a favour — pass me the rivets from that tool kit of mine, will you? Look at these old nails — barely holding on. Leave 'em like this and she'll shake herself apart in no time.
(You follow his gesture, find the rivets, and hand them over.)
Cheers, kiddo. Right then... ha! Done!
Aye. Mr Qiu brought me in to patch this old tub up a bit. Man like him could build a few hundred new ones, yet he clings to this battered heap — funny thing, that.
Best step back, kiddo. I need to saw off this rotten bit — noisy work. Don't want you going half-deaf on my account.
Best patch that seam up soon... leave her soaking a few more months and the core'll rot clean through.
She's old, aye — but good timber lasts. Treat her right and she'll see out a few more decades yet.
Ah, you're back, kiddo. Got questions in that head of yours, or just here to shoot the breeze with an old carpenter?
Quite a few new faces in Haze Market of late — far too chatty when they trade. No class whatsoever.
Tell me about it. Saw this fine little trinket at a stall the other day — thought I'd buy it for the missus. So I asked the price, and guess what he said?
Let me guess — "family heirloom," "dug up from a tomb," one of those tales best left untold.
Worse — breaks the Market's rules! Everyone knows the golden line here: talk price, not provenance. Trade the goods, never the tale behind them.
Ha! That reminds me — a few greenhorns at my stall the other day, calling out prices in the open. Not a whisper of code between them. No respect for the rules at all!
Next time I meet Mr Qiu, it'll have to be somewhere respectable — a proper teahouse, not... whatever this place is.

Having to come down to Haze Market every now and then... dreadful for one's reputation! If anyone were to see me here, I'd never live it down — they'd say I was rubbing shoulders with crooks and swindlers!
You've got quite the opinion of Haze Market.

And who might you be? You don't look like one of the locals... Wait, are you from Mr Qiu's Archaeological Society? No, no, that can't be it — those students never carry anything half as dangerous-looking as that sword of yours.

So what exactly are you after, then? I'll have you know I'm one of Mr Qiu's honoured guests — here to discuss business! No need to go flashing that sword about. And just so you're aware — I'm carrying a Lunarose sachet!

options.content: If you despise Haze Market so much, why do business with Mr Qiu?

talks.content: Jumpy? Nonsense! I simply know better than to trust the sort that lurk around these streets. If you're not one of them, take my advice — keep your wits about you, or they'll have you fleeced before you know it.
Mr Qiu... he's different.
Off already? But you never told me what brings you here!
But if you are one of them... well — forget I said anything!

options.content: So you really despise the people of Haze Market?

talks.content: He's a man of real talent — everyone in business, every collector worth his salt, knows his name. More than that, he's a pleasure to deal with — it's like he sees straight through you.
Hmph! That lot — lawless ruffians, the sort who treat lives like weeds. The dregs of Huaxu — rot that's poisoned its very morals!
There's a saying — when you work with clever folk, you never need to finish your words. They'll catch your meaning and see it done before you even ask.
"Haze Market," they call it — nothing but a den of thieves and thugs! There's no honour among them — they'll chase any coin, however dirty. Pfah! As if any of them still knew what a conscience was!
Oh, plenty! Mr Qiu's generous to a fault — every batch of aged tangerine peel he buys off me is over a hundred years old! Not many in Huaxu can afford such treasures, I can tell you that.
Best keep your distance. Don't be taken in by their polite faces and fine clothes — every one of them's got blood on his hands.

options.content: But isn't Mr Qiu one of them too?
You really think Mr Qiu's clean?

talks.content: He even funds archaeology out of his own pocket! Without his support, half of Huaxu's glorious past would still be buried underground, never seeing daylight.
No, no — Mr Qiu's the exception! He's only here to keep that rabble in line, to stop them doing all those wicked, heartless things. He's the only decent soul in this pit.

Mr Qiu's like a lotus rising from the muck — pure and untouched by the filth around him! To stay that clean in a place like this, and still make a name for himself... remarkable, truly remarkable. You're too young to understand.
And besides that... let me think...

options.content: All right, all right — I get it, you're a hardcore fan of his.

talks.content: Generous, that's what he is! Those of us who deal with him often — every festival, every holiday — Mr Qiu never forgets us. One time it's fine pastries, another time rare curios... he's thoughtful like that, always is.

A what now? "Hardcore"? You young folk and your bizarre jargon — half the time I've no idea what you're on about! Just like my eight-year-old, always tossing around some new term... what was it she said the other day—?
If he weren't so good to us, do you think I'd drag myself all the way down to this wretched place just to wait on him?
Speaking of my little girl — she's quite taken with Mr Qiu herself! Whenever he visits, he brings her sweets, fine pastries... she's forever asking when he'll come again.
(Its form flickers between shadow and pale light, as though it's fighting itself.)
Huff...
Rraugh!
(It raises its head, bloodshot eyes meeting yours — whether from pain or the effort of holding itself together, you cannot tell.)
(As your blade flashes, the Bi'an snaps — its body swallowed by darkness as it lunges at you.)
...Groan... grhh... rrhh...
Awoo... whuh... rrhh...
(Before your eyes, the Bi'an takes its own life.)
(The creature collapses at your feet, its final breath fading into silence.)
(You lay the fallen beast to rest, as gently as you can.)
(From dust it rose — and to dust it fades...)
Brr... freezing again. Rotten weather. Everything's frosted up — gears stiff, sensors half-asleep. Oh dear. Mr Qiu'll have to foot the repairs again.
Hmm? Who are you? What are you doing out here? Off you pop, now. This isn't a place ordinary folk are meant to wander!

options.content: You looked as if you needed a hand, so I thought I'd check in.

talks.content: He did? That can't be right. He said the Gritblight Expanse was my brief alone. Before I left he even said— what was it — "no old records, nothing worth digging into," or something along those lines.

Oh, thank you, kind soul! I've been out here so long — camping in the wind and sleeping under the stars — that I'd almost forgotten normal life being existed... apart from those Sable Bi'an prowling around.
Still, you'd best go home and grab a thicker coat. With the swings here you'll be frozen stiff in no time.
Whew. I'd better throw on a couple more layers myself.
Hot one minute, freezing the next... My grandmother always said it used to be spring all round.
Ah—! It's scorching again! Heat makes me tetchy. Ugh, this wretched coat — off you come!
Hey! Who are y— oh, right, I remember you. Back again, are you? Brought a coat this time?

options.content: I don't mind the cold or the heat.

talks.content: Good. You've no idea how absurd this weather gets — teeth chattering one minute, sweating buckets the next. It's crazy.
What? Then you've not seen it at its worst. Give it an hour — teeth chattering one minute, sweating buckets the next. It's crazy.
Aw, don't go! Took me ages to find someone to chat with. If I don't talk to a normal human soon, my tongue'll go rusty.
Ha! You've come to the right person. I've been out here so long I've nearly pieced the whole story together — this place and that blasted Blightening.
What— no place to set the incense? Good job I brought a burner! After risking my neck to get here, it'd be a bit rich to leave empty-handed!

options.content: What are you doing out here? It's dangerous.
Linger any longer and a Sable Bi'an will be along to make a meal of you.

talks.content: I know! Thanks for the warning. That's exactly why I'm here. I'll light a stick of Lunarose for Lord Argent where only the brave venture, and beg Them to purge the Scourge of Zhuyin once and for all!

No need to fret. I know it's dangerous — that's the point. I'm lighting a stick of Lunarose for Lord Argent right here, where only the brave venture, and begging Him to purge the Scourge of Zhuyin for good.

Don't worry about me. I've no weapon, true, but I've got quick legs and a quicker head! It isn't my first time out here. You watch yourself — if a Sable Bi'an shows up, I'll be off like a shot and won't have time to haul you along.
Go on then — don't trouble over me!
Here we are! Once I light the incense, Lord Argent will surely descend and wipe that wicked beast out for good — just like in the old tales!
Huh? You again. You've got nerve, coming back to a place like this.

options.content: I could say the same about you...
I've got other things to do. I should get going.

talks.content: Ha! Fair point. Like I said, I'm quick on my feet. If trouble turns up, I'll be gone before it catches me. You should head out, though — safer that way.

options.content: I don't need to run. I can drive the Sable Bi'an off myself.

talks.content: All right, then. Until fate brings us together again!
Really? Didn't take you for the tough sort. You're not from Huaxu, are you? Your clothes don't look Huaxu, either.
Will you join me in offering incense, then? Two voices together — surely Lord Argent will hear us better.

options.content: Doesn't it feel a bit odd to offer incense out in the middle of nowhere?

talks.content: You don't know the half of it. You know why the skies twist and churn here, don't you? It's because of the Scourge of Zhuyin a hundred years ago. But do you know why that foul beast brought such ruin on Huaxu?
(You take a stick of incense and join him in the offering.)

options.content: So you mean to call Lord Argent the way people did in the old tales?

talks.content: All right, I won't keep you guessing. Long ago in Huaxu, there lived a wicked creature called Zhuyin.

That's right. These days everyone's burning incense everywhere — Lord Argent must catch it from all sides and hardly know who needs It most! So I figured if I burn mine here, where no one ever comes, It'll take notice.
It sowed unrest in people's hearts and drove them to harm one another. The land fell into misery and people knew no peace, so they lit incense — one after another — and prayed for Lord Argent's help.
Take notice of what, exactly?
On high, Lord Argent caught the scent of the incense, learned of Zhuyin's crime, and grew wrathful. It called on Its divine might and banished the beast beyond Huaxu's shores.
That there's incense burning in the middle of nowhere, of course! They'll see how sincere my heart is!
Then the immortals of the Xuanheng Sect combined their strength, bound Zhuyin with the Loong Seal, and sealed it upon the sacred mountain. Only then did Huaxu know peace again.

options.content: So you mean to call Lord Argent the way people did in the old tales?

talks.content: Right, enough chatter. Will you light another stick with me?
Great! Incense side by side today — fast friends tomorrow!
Fair enough — outsiders don't always get our ways.
The best brews? You'll find them at The Asphodel, no question.
Intoxicating aroma, full-bodied flavours, and what sets it apart most? The smooth, clean finish — it lingers on the tongue.
A fine drink is like a seductive lover... Ah, I think I need another refill...
There's more to The Asphodel than just great drinks.
Because you can enjoy a tipple here without having to worry about getting caught in a brawl with drunkards or getting whacked by some random lunatic...
After all, this is Camilla's turf. Her name alone keeps everyone in line — no one dares stir up trouble here.
Boohoo... Boohoo...
Love... what does it really taste like!? Was it the rush of ecstasy when I joined Camilla's fan club, or the crushing heartbreak when I heard she disbanded it?
Boohoo... Only Lady Camilla's smile can piece back together my shattered heart!
What!? Again...? Can't you just fail once? Fine, fine... guess it still needs a bit more work.
Yep, that's more like it! Honestly? Still not sure what practical use it has... but hey, gotta be good for something.
I gave this thing another upgrade — go on, give it a whirl and help me test the tweaks. Cost me a fortune to smuggle in from Elysium, y'know. No way you're getting through this time!
You're back. Good timing — I gave it another upgrade. Last one was way too easy. But this time? I bet you'll trip at least once.
Again!? Seriously!? I've poured so much into upgrading this thing... But I'm not giving up! Just you wait — I'll get you next time!
Hah! Watching you flail around just now gave me an idea. I'll pitch it to my superior — slap this baby on the Icelake gates and stop anyone from barging in!
There you are! I've been waiting. I poured every last coin into this baby — she's a beast now. No way you're getting through this time.
Again!? Are you kidding me!? Ugh... Y'know what, forget it. I should've known better than to trust Elysian tech. This is what I get for smuggling their junk behind His Majesty's back.

Ha! Gotcha at last! This thing's a masterpiece — I oughta present it to His Majesty himself. Perfect for screening recruits. I'll finally rake in a fat bonus and pay off all the debt I racked up building it.
(The machine hums softly. A crude dial sits atop it, etched with three labels: Easy, Hard, and Extremely Hard. Looks like the handiwork of that overly chatty soldier.)
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
That's right! You picked the right colour — so in you go!
Nope! Have another think. A really good one this time!
Eeya~ Better count again, just to be sure!
So was it the cars that came first... or Catizz?
That's right! You picked the right colour — so in you go!
Nope! Have another think. A really good one this time!
Eeya~ Better count again, just to be sure!
So was it the cars that came first... or Catizz?
(Looks like it is planning to stay at the Sanctuary. Time to give it a name.)
Have you come across any treasures lately? Show me, and I might forge a truly extraordinary weapon out of it!
That's my little friend. Tiny, but strong — it keeps the forge fire going.
Ah! I... I wasn't slacking off... Ahem! I mean, what can I get you?
... (Lunoeggy writes on the board: "So glad you're here!")

options.content: I feel like I've seen you somewhere before...
Have we met in a place called Icelake?

talks.content: ... (That's right! It's me! I've got loads and loads of copies of myself. If you don't believe me, just wait until you reach the next city — you'll see another me there.)
A Lunoeggy with countless copies... what an incredible little creature.

options.content: So... can you open the eggshell and show me what's inside?

talks.content: You're just different Lunos hiding inside the same sort of eggshell, aren't you? You just happened to pick matching shells, for some reason.
...! (Absolutely not! Under this eggshell is another eggshell, and under that is another one! Definitely not a Luno... definitely not!)
... (Hah! That's because the best hiding place is in a crowd of me!)
... (That way, when one of me beats you at dice and you try to win your money back... you'll never know which one it was!)
That actually makes sense.

options.content: So... can you open the eggshell and show me what's inside?

talks.content: Hey! Look who it is — Snow the Demon King and her trusty Loongscion! You came to see me!
I have a name.
Haha, I know! Just messing with you, {nickname}! You're a good friend of mine too! And that red horn of yours — like a pretty maple leaf — I'm sooo jealous, I want one too!
Hey, Lunocarp, what's that tall machine stuffed with all those little balls?
You're really sharp, Snow the Demon King! Spotted the good stuff straight away! This here is my secret money-maker!
I went to a craftsman from the Jishu Sect — Master Gong... Gong-something — and had him build this Lucky Egg machine for me! Toss in a token and — pop! — out comes a random prize!
The trick is letting randomness work its wonders — that's how you make money! This genius idea hit me while I was praying to Lord Argent. Amazing, right?
So... is business any good?
...Meh. Only so-so.
It's just too ahead of its time, so I still haven't made back what I spent on it. Guess that's the fate of a true genius.
Anyway... if you pick up any Taixu Runes, gears, or stuff like that around Mistwharf, you can use them for a spin on my Lucky Egg machine.
These little pieces of useless rubbi— um, I mean, the prizes! Whatever comes out, it's yours! Think of it as a little gift from me!
Hey, it's {nickname} and Snow the Demon King! You came to visit me again! I've got brand-new Lucky Eggs today — wanna give it a spin?

options.content: Ask Lunocarp about her business ideas.

talks.content: Me? I used to be just a plain old Luno, trying every day to squeeze a few more orders out of those stingy Starweavers. But then Snow the Demon King showed up — and she changed my life!
Ooh, about that — I had an epiphany lately! The Lucky Egg isn't just struggling because it's ahead of its time — the real problem is that the prizes are boring! That's the fatal flaw!
I'm not the same Luno I used to be! I'm gonna become a Starweaver whose name goes down in history — and bring the Lunos back to glory!
Some Starweavers in Huaxu made deals with the Xuanheng Sect to sell limited-edition sachets, and they're selling like crazy! That totally inspired me!
Someday, right next to the Demon King's palace, there'll be a huge, fancy shop with my name on it — absolutely!
And if we're talking irresistibly adorable prizes, it's obviously us Lunos!
It's both a dream and a promise! Just you wait — I'll make it happen!
If I make a collab with the Demon King and put it in as the secret rare drop — it's gonna be a massive hit, right? What do you think, {nickname}?
Okay, okay, off you go — you've got things to do! And I've got dreams to chase too... no way I'm falling behind!
Haha! I'll be rolling in coins till I'm dizzy!

name: Captain of "May the Holy Light Shield You"

talks.content: Don't push yourself too hard. We still have to save some strength for those Filthoids.
It's done... Argh...
<W>Your hands are drenched in wet, slimy filth, uncertain whether it's the Filthoid's secretions or its innards. Yet, a sudden joy tingles through your soul, bringing an inexplicable elation.</>

options.content: (Shut up! That was not how I felt!)

talks.content: <W>Do not resist, because I am what you actually are. I am your instinct for death. One day you shall follow my lead and obey the ancient will...</>

options.content: (You refuse to let the ramblings erode your will and try to stay sane.)
